findings.title: D4 and D5: An answered launch of one model will lift the cooldown for other models sharing the same quota key while the quota is still spent
findings.why: D3 groups multiple models under a single QuotaKey (e.g. `antigravity/gemini` covers Flash and Pro; `antigravity/3p` covers Opus, Sonnet, GPT-OSS). Under D4 and D5, an outcome of Ok on any invocation calls Lift(key). When a quota is spent and multiple models share that key, if a cached or concurrent launch completes Ok or if one model is invoked and succeeds right as the window opens, or if a user switches models during a round where one succeeded before the quota was reached, D5 states that in the round aggregate: 'per key, a qualifying spent outcome WINS over a sibling Ok in either order... a key with an Ok and no qualifying refusal is lifted'. If an unaffected row (or a run where only one model failed with a transient error and another succeeded) executes in a subsequent round while the quota remains exhausted, any Ok outcome for that key immediately wipes the standing cooldown file entry via Lift(key), re-enabling all parked models under that key prematurely on the very next round, re-triggering 30-minute hangs.
findings.fix: Ensure Lift(key) is only performed when an actual live call to the same model or family explicitly proves the quota is available, or verify that Ok outcomes do not lift a standing cooldown unless the quota gauge itself reports Available or the standing cooldown's UntilUtc has elapsed.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. No code defect seen: D4's lift rule (a live answer overrules a closed door) is deliberate, and a parked key's rows are excluded from the next round, so only a concurrent launch can lift it; the code lifts only when an entry stands (R4).

findings.title: D5 and D6: Running the /quota probe with the same execution environment and working directory will fail when called outside an authenticated review session
findings.why: D6 states that AgyQuotaProbe reuses the failed invocation's Request (same executable, environment, and working directory AntigravityReadOnly.Home()). However, when agy runs under AntigravityReadOnly.Home(), agy CLI commands like /quota require access to user configuration, session auth tokens, and credentials that may only exist in the user's real home directory ($HOME) or via specific authentication cookies/tokens. If AntigravityReadOnly.Home() isolates or masks the real user HOME directory to enforce read-only execution, `agy -p /quota` cannot read authentication state and exits non-zero with an authentication/login error, resulting in CannotCheck and causing spent quotas to always fall back to the 30-minute doubling guess rather than obtaining the real reset_time.
findings.fix: Specify the exact requirements for environment variables (such as HOME, USERPROFILE, and auth tokens) needed by `agy -p /quota` in AntigravityReadOnly.Home(), and add a scenario verifying that AgyQuotaProbe can resolve user authentication when running in that isolated working directory.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. No code defect seen: the probe reuses the failed invocation's own Request, the very environment and home in which the review launch just authenticated, and the plan records two real agy 1.4.9 captures as fixtures.

findings.title: D3 and D6: Models table and bucket ID mappings omit Claude 4.6 and other current models
findings.why: D3 explicitly defines model family matching by stripping trailing `-low`, `-medium`, `-high` from IDs like `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gemini-3.8-flash`. According to D3, unknown families never query `/quota` ('no inferred group; no gauge-based parking'), causing all 4.x models configured on agy to default to text-only stated/guess wait times instead of using the `/quota` gauge.

findings.title: PanelService creates QuotaCooldowns without passing its IProcessLauncher dependency
findings.why: PanelService instantiates `_cooldowns = new QuotaCooldowns(settings.DataDir, _clock, log, launcher, noticing.Offer);` where the parameter `launcher` is not defined or in scope in `PanelService.cs` (or defaults to null / creates a NoLauncherAvailable). Consequently, any spent Antigravity quota in real rounds throws `InvalidOperationException("this store was given no launcher")` inside `ReadResetAsync`, failing to run `agy -p /quota` and degrading every spent agy cooldown to an unread probe or guess.
findings.fix: Pass the existing runtime/scheduler `IProcessLauncher` instance into `QuotaCooldowns` when constructing it in `PanelService`.
findings.reason: Wrong; opened PanelService.cs: `launcher` is the constructor parameter at line 65 (the same one handed to the executor, scheduler and context assembler), and line 110 passes it to QuotaCooldowns. The round-level test ASpentQuotaOfARoundCoolsTheRowForTheNextOneTests runs a real review_plan round through PanelService with a scripted agy launcher and asserts the /quota reset (2026-10-14T07:19:16) lands in the file, which could not pass with NoLauncher.

findings.title: Applying changes compares state against unpruned read and fails to write expired entry drops
findings.why: In `WriteLocked`, `read` contains all raw entries from disk (including expired entries), while `next` starts by filtering `read.Where(entry => entry.UntilUtc > now).ToList()`. When `changes` contains only a `Lift` for an already absent/expired key, or when applying changes produces entries identical to the expired-pruned set, `next.SequenceEqual(read)` compares the pruned list against the unpruned `read`. If the only changes to the file are expired entries that should be pruned on write (as mandated by DoD #10), `next.SequenceEqual(read)` evaluates to false, but if `changes` is empty or no-op while expired entries exist, pruning never executes. Conversely, if `read` had expired entries and a new change was added, `next.SequenceEqual(read)` is false and writes out `next`, but comparing `next` (pruned) to `read` (unpruned) means `SequenceEqual` is checking two structurally different lists with different lifetimes, making change detection leaky across pruning boundaries.
findings.fix: Prune expired entries on `read` before determining change equality or check whether `read` has expired entries when evaluating `SequenceEqual` against pruned `read`.
findings.reason: Wrong; the comparison is deliberate. In WriteLocked `next` is the pruned set plus the changes and `read` is the raw file, so an expired entry on disk makes them differ and the write happens and drops it (DoD: every write drops entries past untilUtc, S20). Comparing against a pruned `read` would make a no-op change skip the write and keep the expired entry. Apply is only called with at least one change, so there is no empty-changes case.

findings.title: Lift decision is ignored if any rate limit occurs on a shared quota key
findings.why: In `DecisionAsync`, `limited.Count > 0 && await ParkAsync(...)` is evaluated before checking `LiftOf`. If one model under a shared quota key (such as `antigravity/gemini`) encounters a transient rate limit or an undecided rate limit where `ParkAsync` returns `null` (e.g. transient 429 where `reset is not QuotaReset.Parked`), `DecisionAsync` immediately falls through to `LiftOf`. However, if `ParkAsync` returns a `park` change (even from an estimate/guess or stale error) while a sibling model on the same quota key succeeded with `ReviewerOutcome.Ok`, `ParkAsync` completely overrides the answered launch. While DoD rule states a spent refusal wins over Ok, if the refusal was transient/not parked, but `limited` had entries, the method properly checks LiftOf only on `park == null`. But in `ParkAsync`, `limited.OrderBy(pair => Rank(...)).First()` picks the top refusal without verifying whether sibling `Ok` occurred when `refusal.Spent == null` (undecided), causing a transient refusal to potentially park or block lift evaluation improperly across family members.
findings.fix: Ensure `DecisionAsync` explicitly coordinates the precedence between `Ok` and `limited` according to `Spent` status, returning `LiftOf` whenever all limited outcomes are non-spent and an `Ok` is present.
findings.reason: Wrong against the code and D5. DecisionAsync parks only when ParkAsync returns a Parked reset, which D10 never gives for a transient or undecided refusal (QuotaReset.NotParked); it then falls through to LiftOf, which lifts on an Ok. Rank puts a spent refusal first, so an undecided sibling never speaks for the key over a spent one. A spent refusal winning over a sibling Ok is the plan's explicit rule (S35-S37), and both orders are covered by the existing tests.

findings.title: Probe executes inside target repository working directory instead of a safe neutral directory
findings.why: AgyQuotaProbe copies invocation.Request directly (with only arguments, stdin, timeout and track-as modified), preserving WorkingDirectory from the reviewer launch. If the round is reviewing a repository containing untrusted code or git hooks, executing `agy -p /quota` inside that untrusted working tree crosses trust boundaries or risks unexpected tool behavior/side effects in user space.
findings.fix: Set WorkingDirectory on the probe request to Path.GetTempPath() or a dedicated scratch directory rather than inheriting invocation.Request.WorkingDirectory.
findings.reason: Wrong; the probe does not run in the target repository. The agy request's working directory is AntigravityReadOnly.Home() (AntigravityRuntime.cs:64), the neutral read-only agent home; the checkout is passed only as the --add-dir workspace argument, which the probe replaces with its own arguments. D6 of the plan names this home as the intended working directory.

findings.title: Cooldown writes do not enforce 16 KiB size budget or prune entries on read-only cycles
findings.why: Definition of Done requirement 10 states 'quota-cooldowns.json has a budget: one entry per key, entries past their untilUtc dropped on every write, under 16 KiB'. The implementation never checks or enforces the 16 KiB ceiling on serialized output before or during write, allowing corrupted/bloated inputs or notes to exceed the budget silently.
findings.fix: Assert or guard that the serialized JSON byte length does not exceed 16384 bytes prior to calling AtomicFile.Write, refusing the write or trimming entries if it exceeds the budget.
findings.reason: Covered by design (plan section 8, S20): the file is a set with one entry per key, keys come from D3's finite table plus one per unknown agy model a person configures (under ten in any real settings file), each note is capped at 400 characters (about 600 bytes an entry), and every write drops expired entries; S20 asserts ten 400-character notes stay under 16 KiB. The 16 KiB is a projected ceiling that this bound guarantees, not a runtime limit the plan asks for; a size guard that refuses a park would lose a real cooldown, which the plan says never to do. Adding a runtime cap is a plan change.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse splits only on LF, breaking on CRLF lines
findings.why: On Windows platforms where stderr may contain CRLF ('\r\n') line endings, splitting on '\n' with StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries leaves trailing '\r' handled depending on parser trimming, but when slicing line[Marker.Length..].TrimStart(':', ' ', '\t') in OneLine, any trailing '\r' remains at the end of the JSON string, causing JsonDocument.Parse to fail on malformed JSON tokens.
findings.fix: Use stderr.Split(['\r', '\n'], StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries | StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries) or trim '\r' in OneLine before JSON parsing.
findings.reason: Wrong; the stderr is split on '\n' with StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries, which trims all whitespace including a trailing '\r', so a CRLF line reaches JsonDocument.Parse without it. Not a defect.

findings.title: PanelService re-reads and parses quota-cooldowns.json from disk per provider row on every CanRun check
findings.why: CooldownEntryOf is called unmemoized multiple times per row during every probe or round launch (in CanRun, in CooldownOf, in ExcludedFrom, in RosterBuilder, etc.). CooldownEntryOf calls QuotaCooldowns.Standing(), which executes File.ReadAllText and JsonSerializer.Deserialize on every single call without caching or checking file timestamps/mtimes. With 10–20 configured provider rows and frequent 10s UI polls or multi-stage round planning, this performs dozens to hundreds of redundant disk reads and JSON parsing passes per round cycle, creating an N+1 disk I/O pattern on hot scheduling paths.
findings.fix: Cache the parsed QuotaCooldownFile in memory inside QuotaCooldowns with the file's LastWriteTimeUtc / file version, invalidating or re-reading from disk only when the file modification time changes or when an in-process write occurs.
findings.reason: By design: plan section 8 says several coai-mcp processes on one data directory read the file on every decision so a park by one is seen by the others on the next round (S17, S28). The file is at most a few hundred bytes to a few KB, read on a UI poll or a round start, not a hot loop; an mtime cache would add a stale-read window across processes that the plan rules out and is outside the plan's scope. No measurement shows a cost.

findings.title: Quota probe timeout of 30 seconds can stall AfterRoundAsync completion with no round progress feedback
findings.why: When an Antigravity model hits quota exhaustion, RoundEngine calls AfterRoundAsync, which runs AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync before returning round results. If the agy CLI hangs or its backend network connection stalls, the user and UI wait an extra 30 seconds after all reviewer launches have completed, with no UI status or progress indication explaining why the round has not finished.
findings.fix: Reduce Bound to 10 seconds (or run the probe asynchronously in the background / detached after posting the round result, using Stated / Guess immediately if the probe doesn't return quickly).
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope and by design: D6/section 8 fix the probe at one agy child per spent key per round bounded at 30 s by the launcher, run after the reviewers finished so a spent quota never costs the 30 minutes #878 is about. The probe only runs when a quota is actually spent, and a failed or slow probe falls back to the stated text or coai's own guess. Moving it to the background would change the plan's contract that the park is decided before the summary (the next round must see it); a 10 s bound is a plan change.

findings.title: AgyQuotaReport.Parse splits entire stdout into lines and attempts JsonDocument.Parse on every line
findings.why: When stdout is not a single valid JSON document (e.g., when agy outputs streaming logs or verbose text interspersed with JSON), Documents() calls stdout.Split('\n') and runs JsonDocument.Parse inside a try/catch block for every line. For large outputs with many lines, throwing and catching JsonException repeatedly allocates substantial garbage and degrades runtime performance.
findings.fix: Filter candidate lines before calling JsonDocument.Parse (e.g. check for leading '{' or '[' after trimming) so JsonException is not thrown on every plain text line.
findings.reason: Not observable and not a defect: `agy -p /quota --output-format json` prints one JSON document; the per-line fallback only runs when that whole-text parse fails, on output capped by the launcher's 30 s bound. A try/catch per line costs microseconds at this size and no test can fail for the right reason, so there is nothing to put red first; a micro-optimisation outside the plan.

findings.title: The cooldown file has no enforced size limit
findings.why: The store caps each note and keeps one entry per key, but it never limits the number of keys or the serialized file size. If many distinct unknown model IDs are configured and each gets parked, successive writes can grow `quota-cooldowns.json` beyond the stated 16 KiB budget; later reads deserialize the whole file on every standing check, increasing disk and memory use without bound.
findings.fix: Before writing, enforce the 16 KiB serialized-size limit and refuse the write explicitly when the next file would exceed it; also reject oversized files before deserializing.
findings.reason: Duplicate of finding 4 (same line, same claim) and rejected for the same reason: the budget is held by the key set, the 400-character note cap and the drop-expired-on-write rule (S20); a runtime refusal would lose a real cooldown, and a read-time size check is a plan change for a file in the person's own data directory.

findings.title: Quota probes run serially and can delay the round summary without progress feedback.
findings.why: If a round has spent quotas in all three known Antigravity groups and each `/quota` probe times out, `DecidedAsync` awaits them one by one, adding up to 90 seconds before the summary is returned; a contended cooldown lock can add another 30 seconds. The person sees no completion or probe status during that post-review wait.
findings.fix: Run independent per-key probes concurrently while retaining one probe per key, and expose a bounded progress/status update during post-round cooldown work.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope: running the per-key probes one after another is what D5/section 8 specify ('one agy child per spent key per round, bounded at 30 s'). The 90 s worst case needs all three agy groups spent in one round and every probe hanging to its bound; concurrency would also change the order of the log and the aggregate the tests pin. A follow-up optimisation, not a defect of this change; the lock wait is already taken off the round's thread (R3).

findings.title: D6 can treat an unreadable quota bucket as proof that the whole group is available
findings.why: If an agy refusal is undecided and the weekly bucket has a missing or invalid remaining_fraction while the 5h bucket reports a positive fraction, the plan explicitly skips the unreadable bucket and returns Available. AfterRoundAsync then parks nothing, so the next round launches the quota-limited model again even though the gauge could not establish that its weekly allowance was available.
findings.fix: Return a cannot-check result whenever any active bucket needed to establish availability is unreadable; only return Available when every relevant active bucket is readable and positive, and add a scenario for one unreadable bucket alongside one positive bucket.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Checked in code: AgyQuotaReport.ResetFor skips an unreadable bucket exactly as D6 says, and an undecided refusal with an Available gauge parks nothing by design; the code matches the plan, it is not a code defect.)

Because no scenario test drives or verifies RoundEngine actually calling AfterRoundAsync, a wiring error, unawaited task, or omission in RoundEngine allows the entire round flow to complete without ever executing AfterRoundAsync, leaving quota-cooldowns.json unwritten and repeating the 30-minute launch penalty on the next round.

findings.why: D9 specifies: 'the card's foot draws it as cooldown-line INSTEAD of the ledger's reset-line while a cooldown stands'. When a row is cooling down, any existing token count, cost, or recent usage metrics displayed by the ledger reset-line are completely masked and unavailable to the user until the cooldown expires.

findings.title: Quota keys cross the runtime boundary as untyped strings
findings.why: The C# doctrine says: “A business concept does not travel as a `string` or an `int`. Wrap it in a typed value with parsing and validation (`CommitSha`, `RepoUrl`, `Email`). Parsing lives in a static factory returning a result value — never a throwing constructor, because a malformed input is an expected answer.” `QuotaKeyOf` returns `string`, and those values are passed between runtimes, cooldown decisions, and storage; they are not merely HTTP/JSON/JS-interop IDs. This lets arbitrary or malformed keys enter the quota boundary without validation.
findings.fix: Introduce a quota-key value type with a result-returning parser, and use it in `QuotaKeyOf` and the cooldown service boundary.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope and a plan decision: D3 defines the quota key as an explicit string (it is also the persisted JSON key and the wire member, and QuotaCooldowns/AgyQuotaGroups are its only producers, from a closed table). A typed QuotaKey would touch every runtime and the wire and is a refactor the plan did not ask for.

findings.title: The quota fixture helper mutates its parsed JSON tree
findings.why: The coding-style rule says: “ALWAYS create new objects, NEVER mutate existing ones.” `Edited` parses a JSON tree and then passes that same tree to an `Action<JsonNode>` that edits it in place; the test cases use this helper to mutate existing nodes and properties.
findings.fix: Build each edited fixture as a new JSON value rather than changing the parsed tree in place.
findings.reason: Wrong: Edited(string json, Action<JsonNode>) parses a fresh tree from the immutable input string, edits that private local copy and returns a new string; no shared or existing object is mutated and the input is unchanged. Test-only helper, no defect.

findings.title: A successful launch is considered an answer even when its result is malformed or contains no review.
findings.why: After an earlier spend is parked, a sibling row sharing the key can return `ReviewerOutcome.Ok` despite an invalid or unusable response. `answered` then lifts the cooldown, so the next round launches the spent quota again even though no valid review proved that the account was usable.
findings.fix: Only treat an `Ok` as an answer when the executor has validated and accepted its review payload; otherwise preserve the standing cooldown.
findings.reason: Wrong: ReviewerOutcome.Ok carries a NormalisedReview — the executor has already parsed and accepted a review payload before an outcome is Ok; a malformed or empty answer is a different outcome (not Ok). D4 says an answered launch lifts the cooldown.

findings.title: A quota gauge failure can erase an existing cooldown without a successful launch.
findings.why: If a key already has a standing cooldown and its new launch returns an undecided refusal, `SettledAsync` enters `ParkedAsync`; when the probe cannot run, `Parks` returns false and `Quiet(key, answered)` produces `Nothing`. The subsequent locked write drops expired entries only, so the existing unexpired entry remains in this instance, but the uncertain refusal also provides no refresh; more critically, an answer from the gauge marked available also returns `Nothing`. If the stored reset is stale or the gauge is inconsistent during a real spent refusal, the row may remain parked only until its prior time and then be retried despite the spent state.
findings.fix: When a standing cooldown exists, preserve or extend it on inconclusive/available gauge results; only lift it on an answered launch.
findings.reason: Wrong: opened SettledAsync/ParkedAsync/Quiet. An inconclusive or Available gauge returns Quiet(key, answered), which is Lift only when a launch of the key ended Ok, otherwise Nothing — a standing entry is neither erased nor changed (the finding itself says the entry remains). Extending a park on an inconclusive gauge would invent a date, which the plan forbids (S24: a failed check parks nothing it did not already know).

findings.title: Unreadable cooldown files are silently treated as no cooldown on read.
findings.why: If another process or an attacker makes `quota-cooldowns.json` unreadable, `Standing` returns no entry and the provider becomes runnable. This avoids wrongly parking a working account, but also means a spent quota can be retried repeatedly while the persistence error continues; the warning only occurs if the exception reaches this catch and may expose its filesystem message in logs.
findings.fix: Keep the fail-open policy, but ensure read failures are surfaced to the operator through the same storage notice path as refused writes.
findings.reason: By design and already covered: D4 'the fail-open contract' and S19/S37 — a bad or unreadable file must never park a working account; the read warns once per process. The write side (H1 fix 0484298f) refuses and says so as a notice. Surfacing read failures as a notice is an extra beyond the plan.

findings.title: Quota gauge probes run sequentially for every spent key in the round.
findings.why: If a round has ten simultaneously spent quota keys, `ParkAndLiftAsync` awaits each 30-second `/quota` probe before starting the next, so post-round processing can delay the response by up to five minutes and the person waits without a completion update.
findings.fix: Run independent per-key reset reads concurrently, with a bounded concurrency limit, then apply all decisions in the single locked write.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope: D5/D6 specify one /quota probe per spent key per round, each bounded by the launcher's 30 s tree-killing timeout. The number of probed keys is at most the three agy groups of D3's table (an unknown key is not probed, other runtimes do no I/O), so the worst case is bounded; concurrency is an optimisation the plan did not ask for and would complicate the single locked write.

findings.title: PanelService creates a private QuotaCooldowns instance rather than resolving it from DI alongside usage tracking and store infrastructure
findings.why: PanelService instantiates `new QuotaCooldowns(...)` inline and threads it only into RoundEngine. Any future consumer or sibling coordinator (such as QuestionConsultService, CadenceDesk, FeatureStage, or the upcoming 'PLAN_a_cooldown_reaches_every_road' consultation/check/api runners explicitly called out in module_runners.md) cannot see, inject, or respect the cooldown state unless they are either wired through PanelService or instantiate duplicate QuotaCooldowns stores reading and locking the same file separately. This hardwires runner lifecycle and storage coordination directly into a UI-facing presentation service, creating an inverted layer dependency.
findings.fix: Extract IQuotaCooldowns / QuotaCooldowns registration to the runner / service composition root where UsageLedger and other shared stores are constructed, and inject it into PanelService and RoundEngine as a shared dependency.
findings.reason: Wrong/out of scope: PanelService IS this repository's composition root for the round stack — it builds UsageLedger, CallerSessions, Escalations, CadenceStore the same way on the neighbouring lines — and QuotaCooldowns is built once and shared with RoundEngine and the card. Extending the cooldown to consultation/check/api roads is explicitly the later plan PLAN_a_cooldown_reaches_every_road (D12), not this change.

findings.title: QuotaCooldowns reaches into invocation.Adapter to trigger asynchronous probe I/O, creating an inverted runtime orchestration dependency
findings.why: QuotaCooldowns is a state storage and persistence aggregate ('one small file quota-cooldowns.json'). In SettledAsync / ParkedAsync, it assumes the responsibility of driving I/O probes across vendors by invoking `chosen.Invocation.Adapter!.ReadResetAsync(...)` with an injected process launcher. A storage component should not orchestrate CLI executions or vendor communications; when new runtime adapters or probing strategies are introduced, QuotaCooldowns must change, violating Single Responsibility and leaking runtime execution concerns into store persistence.
findings.fix: Separate cooldown resolution from storage: let a quota probe coordinator or the round engine resolve the QuotaReset across the round results, and pass the resolved resets into QuotaCooldowns.AfterRoundAsync (or RecordCooldownsAsync) purely as data to be evaluated and persisted.
findings.reason: Plan decision (D4/D5): the store decides park/lift per key and asks the chosen invocation's adapter for the reset (ReadResetAsync) because the persisted entry needs the reset, source and note together under one locked write. Splitting a probe coordinator out is a refactor beyond the plan; no defect shown.

findings.title: AgyQuotaGroups statically couples model ID strings to Antigravity quota buckets, bypassing model configuration abstraction
findings.why: AgyQuotaGroups hardcodes specific model string literals ('gemini-3.8-flash', 'claude-opus-5-5', etc.) and bucket names in a static array Table. When an operator configures an aliased model, a newly released preview model, or a model via custom settings in PanelSettings, KeyOf falls back to UnknownPrefix ('antigravity/?...'). Because AntigravityRuntime.ReadResetAsync explicitly skips /quota probing when the key starts with UnknownPrefix (line 188), any new or configured model on Antigravity will silently bypass gauge probing and always degrade to a 30-minute fallback guess, requiring code changes to a static runner class for routine model additions.
findings.fix: Make quota family classification extensible via provider/runtime metadata or model family prefix mapping instead of an unconfigurable static array of full model names.
findings.reason: Plan decision, not a defect: D3 is explicit that agy keys come from ONE explicit measured table 'never a prefix' (Argon's ids start gemini- too, so a prefix rule would park every Gemini row when only Argon is spent), and an unknown family gets its own key and is simply not probed (S14, the issue's unknown group). Adding a family is one row plus a fixture, as the code's remarks say.

findings.title: Double iteration over results enumerable with different C# lambda targets causes inconsistent state
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.ParkedAsync`, `chosen` is resolved by chaining `.Where(...).Concat(refusals).First()`. If `refusals` contains no elements where `Spent == true`, `chosen` takes the first element of `refusals`. However, in `SettledAsync`, `refusals` is filtered with `p.Outcome is ReviewerOutcome.RateLimited r && Qualifies(r)`, where `Qualifies` evaluates `limited.Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(limited.Reason)`. If an antigravity model produces an undecided refusal (`Spent: null`) where `Hopeless` is true, but then in `ParkedAsync` it calls `chosen.Invocation.Adapter!.ReadResetAsync`, `ReadResetAsync` for `AntigravityRuntime` evaluates `verdict switch`: if `/quota` reports `Available` (`AgyQuotaVerdict.Available`), `ReadResetAsync` returns `fallback with { Gauge = GaugeReading.Available }`. In `Parks(limited, reset)`, `limited.Spent == true || reset.Gauge is GaugeReading.NotAsked or GaugeReading.Spent` evaluates to false (as `limited.Spent` is null and `reset.Gauge` is `Available`), so it does not park. But when `AgyQuotaProbe` fails with `CannotCheck`, `reset.Gauge` is `GaugeReading.CannotCheck`. In `Parks`, `GaugeReading.CannotCheck` evaluates to false (`reset.Gauge is GaugeReading.NotAsked or GaugeReading.Spent` is false), returning `Quiet(key, answered)` and never parking. However, if multiple refusals exist in the group (e.g. one `Spent: null` and one `Spent: false`), `chosen` could pick one arbitrarily or fail to inspect remaining refusals that actually had decisive gauge/verdict outcomes.
findings.fix: Ensure `chosen` explicitly searches for the most specific refusal (e.g., checking for any definitive spent outcome first) and if multiple refusals exist for a key, do not abandon evaluating other refusals if one yields an unchecked or transient gauge reading.
findings.reason: Wrong: opened ParkedAsync/SettledAsync. refusals is already filtered by Qualifies (Spent ?? Hopeless); chosen prefers a refusal the vendor called Spent==true, else the first. The gauge read is per KEY (not per launch), so which undecided refusal is chosen yields the same /quota reading; a Spent==false refusal never enters refusals. The described inconsistency does not exist.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse drops Windows CRLF formatted stderr lines due to strict '\n' splitting
findings.why: In `AgyError.Parse`, the method splits `stderr` with `stderr.Split('\n', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries | StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)`. In `OfLine(string line)`, it inspects `var json = line[Marker.Length..].TrimStart(':', ' ', '\t');` and then parses with `JsonDocument.Parse(json)`. If `stderr` contains trailing `\r` or Windows CRLF line endings that were not stripped (or if individual JSON chunks have trailing whitespace/newlines before JSON objects), `TrimStart` does not strip `\r`. While `StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries` trims whitespace including `\r`, if `stderr` has embedded multi-line JSON or non-standard carriage returns, parsing fails and returns null, discarding the error and preventing `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` and `Individual quota reached` from being detected on Windows CLI runs.
findings.fix: Use `line.AsSpan()[Marker.Length..].Trim().ToString()` or trim `\r` and whitespace explicitly before `JsonDocument.Parse`.
findings.reason: Wrong: AgyError.Parse splits on '\n' with StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries, which trims a trailing '\r' (the finding says so itself); a CRLF stderr therefore parses. No failing input is given.

findings.title: AtomicFile.Write unhandled exception inside Locked hold can leave the lock held during unexpected write crashes
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.AppliedHolding`, `using (taken.Stream)` handles disposal of the lock stream, but `Applied` directly calls `AtomicFile.Write(FilePath, Serialized(next))`. If `AtomicFile.Write` encounters an unexpected exception that is not `IOException` or `UnauthorizedAccessException` (for example, `OutOfMemoryException` or argument/path format exceptions during temp file renaming), `Mutate`'s catch filter `when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` does not catch it, allowing the exception to propagate out of `Mutate`, though the `using` block disposes the stream. However, in `AfterRoundAsync`, the outer catch catches all exceptions, but leaving behind a partially written temp file on disk without cleanup.
findings.fix: Ensure any temp files created by `AtomicFile.Write` are cleaned up on failure or handle general filesystem exceptions uniformly in `Mutate`.
findings.reason: Not a defect of this change: AtomicFile.Write is the repository's existing helper (temp then move) used as D4 prescribes; an OutOfMemory/format exception is not a case to handle, the lock stream is disposed by the using, and AfterRoundAsync's outer catch already keeps the round's results untouched.

findings.title: Vendor error message written verbatim into persistent quota cooldown file and wire DTO without stripping potential tokens or sensitive URL parameters
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.NoteOf`, `NoteOf` builds the persistent note as `${reset.Note}. Vendor said: ${VendorReason.Written(reason)}` and saves it in `quota-cooldowns.json`, which is then served over `--providers` wire DTO (`CooldownReport.Note`). While `VendorReason.Written` trims or limits certain characters, raw error messages from custom endpoints or vendor CLI stderr might contain bearer tokens, query parameters, internal paths, or confidential prompt snippets returned by the remote API. These secrets become persistently written to disk in plain text and broadcast over the wire to VS Code.
findings.fix: Sanitize or strip sensitive tokens/patterns (such as authorization headers, API keys, and file paths) from `reason` before concatenating into `NoteOf`.
findings.reason: Already covered: NoteOf writes the vendor's sentence through VendorReason.Written, i.e. the product's one redactor (Redaction.SafeText: control characters, key blocks, credential-named values, recognisable shapes) cut at the cap, exactly as D4 says; the same redacted text is what the ledger and the log already keep.

findings.title: Uncached synchronous file reads and deserializations of quota-cooldowns.json in loop over all providers
findings.why: StandingCooldown is invoked by CanRun, IsCooling, CooldownOf, and ExclusionReason for every provider. In PanelService.ProvidersAnswer, CardOf calls CooldownOf (1 read). CanRun calls IsCooling -> StandingCooldown (1 read). When evaluating ExcludedFrom in RosterBuilder/PanelService across all providers (e.g., 10-20 configured providers), each provider check invokes File.ReadAllText and JsonSerializer.Deserialize. For N providers, this triggers 2N to 4N disk reads and JSON parsing passes on quota-cooldowns.json on every single status poll or round evaluation, blocking the request synchronously on the thread pool.
findings.fix: Cache the parsed quota cooldown file in memory (invalidated on write or using a file timestamp / snapshot) or load the cooldown entries once per ProvidersAnswer / BuildWork pass instead of re-reading and re-parsing from disk inside each provider's property getter.
findings.reason: Plan decision: D4 states 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever, §8)' — a cache would have to be invalidated against the writer in another process (the file is lock-shared with the other side). A few reads of a file under 16 KiB per poll is not a defect.

findings.title: Sequential agy probe execution over multiple spent quota keys stalls round completion
findings.why: In QuotaCooldowns.ParkAndLiftAsync, foreach (var group in ...) invokes SettledAsync -> ParkedAsync sequentially with an await in each iteration. If multiple agy keys (e.g. Gemini, Argon, 3p) or multiple providers report rate limits in the same round, each probe runs agy -p '/quota' with a 30s timeout sequentially. With 3 exhausted groups, the round completion waits up to 90 seconds sequentially after reviewer execution has finished before the round results are returned and persisted.
findings.fix: Run probe tasks concurrently across distinct quota keys using Task.WhenAll(groups.Select(g => SettledAsync(...))) before Mutate.
findings.reason: Duplicate of finding 5: the plan specifies one probe per spent key, each bounded by the launcher's timeout; at most the three agy groups can be probed; concurrency is beyond the plan.

findings.title: Rounding logic in QuotaInstants.Left displays confusing hour counts when duration is just over one hour
findings.why: When untilUtc - nowUtc is 61 minutes, minutes is 61. The expression (minutes + 59) / 60 evaluates to (120 / 60) = 2 h. A user seeing 'back at 12:01 (in 2 h)' at 11:00 sees a 1-hour wait represented as 2 hours, which mismatches the clock timestamp shown right next to it.
findings.fix: Use Math.Ceiling(minutes / 60.0) or format as hours and minutes (e.g. 1 h 1 min) when close to the boundary, or align with standard integer ceiling arithmetic.
findings.reason: Wrong: the plan requires the time left 'rounded up' (S31-S33); 61 minutes rounded up to whole hours is 2 h, which is the specified ceiling, and the exact clock time is printed beside it.

findings.title: D5 parks an agy key on a stated or guessed reset when the quota probe cannot check it, so an ordinary model error can suppress a working account for hours.
findings.why: For a spent agy refusal, D2 sets Spent=true from the individual-quota sentence, but D5 says a failed /quota probe falls back to the refusal's stated reset or a guess. If agy returns that sentence alongside a stale or unavailable quota endpoint, the next round excludes the entire quota group until the stated wait (up to the parser's 14-day maximum) even though the plan cannot confirm that quota is exhausted. The separate "cannot check" state says a failed check parks nothing it did not already know, but D5's fallback does exactly that for a newly observed refusal.
findings.fix: Define and test the failed-gauge path for explicit-spent agy refusals consistently: either park only for a bounded, explicitly marked fallback interval with a stated rationale, or leave it unparked until a successful gauge confirms exhaustion.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The park-on-stated-reset fallback is D5's deliberate design for an explicit spent refusal.)

findings.title: Deviation 2 introduces a partial class to split QuotaCooldowns across files, directly violating repository coding style
findings.why: Section 12 item 2 states: 'QuotaCooldowns is one partial class in two files: QuotaCooldowns.cs (the store) and QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs (AfterRoundAsync)'. Coding style rule '.agents/conventions/common/coding-style.md' explicitly forbids this pattern under File Organization: 'split by extracting a named unit with its own responsibility, never a partial (or its equivalent) to duck the limit'. If built or committed as a partial class, it violates non-negotiable coding standards and fails code review / style gating.
findings.fix: Refactor the round-handling logic into a distinct, named collaborating class (e.g., `QuotaCooldownRoundHandler` or `RoundCooldownCoordinator`) rather than splitting `QuotaCooldowns` using `partial`.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. NOTE: the partial class is a real defect in the CODE (QuotaCooldowns.cs + QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs, 415 lines together) against coding-style 'never a partial'; it is fixed in the code, not in the plan.

findings.title: A spent quota refusal that does not emit 'AGY_ERROR' is classified as ByText and never marked Spent: true
findings.why: In §1, Antigravity's quota error format shows two separate outputs: an 'AGY_ERROR: {...}' block on stderr AND a stdout/envelope JSON '{"status": "ERROR", "response": "", "error": "Individual quota reached. ..."}'. In D2, AntigravityRuntime overrides RateLimited to only inspect lines starting with 'AGY_ERROR' in stderr. If Antigravity CLI outputs the error only in stdout (e.g. streaming or format variants) or stderr without the exact 'AGY_ERROR' prefix, D2 falls back to RateLimitVerdict.ByText(result), which leaves Spent as null. Under D5, Spent == null with Hopeless(reason) triggers a gauge check, but if the gauge is unreadable or answers Available, the spent row is not parked despite an explicit Individual Quota Reached failure.
findings.fix: In AgyError.Parse, check both the AGY_ERROR prefix on stderr and the stdout result JSON error field for the 'Individual quota reached' payload, setting Spent: true when either contains the exhaustion signal.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D2 reads only the AGY_ERROR line on purpose; a status=ERROR envelope alone is not evidence of a spent quota.)

findings.title: Unauthenticated or configuration errors during agy /quota probe are swallowed into CannotCheck without triggering existing diagnostic flows
findings.why: In D6 and S15, any probe exit code other than 0 (e.g., exit 1 or 3 due to missing credentials, expired login, or corrupted config in AntigravityReadOnly.Home()) produces CannotCheck(why). In D5, an agy outcome with Spent == null and a probe returning CannotCheck results in 'not parked, the note says could not check', silently ignoring the authentication/quota issue and letting subsequent rounds repeat the failing call loop indefinitely.
findings.fix: Differentiate between transient execution failures and credential/environment failures in AgyQuotaProbe, returning a dedicated status that delegates to VendorDiagnosis or surfaces a clear configuration alert.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Diagnosing agy credential failures is a different feature from the cooldown.)

findings.title: A malformed cooldown file is treated as empty and then overwritten by the next mutation
findings.why: For example, after a torn or unsupported-version file makes `ReadStrict` return `[]`, `Park` builds a new entry and `Rewrite` writes it over the existing file. Any still-valid quota entries in that unreadable document are lost, so a later round launches rows whose quotas were already parked. The plan requires a bad or unreadable file to park nobody, but separately requires that a write based on an unreadable re-read refuse rather than overwrite unknown state.
findings.fix: Distinguish a missing file from an unreadable or invalid file in the locked read; allow missing files to initialize, but return `CooldownWrite.Refused` without writing when an existing file cannot be parsed.
findings.reason: Wrong on the plan: §8 and S19/S37 say a torn or non-version-1 file reads as no cooldown with one warning and is overwritten whole by the next park (a file that merely cannot be parsed holds nothing coai can trust). What must not be overwritten is a file whose READ FAILED: ReadStrict lets IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException propagate to Change, which refuses the write (commit a9c6a30f, test in ASpentQuotaIsRememberedUntilItsResetTests). Both halves are already as the plan has them.

findings.title: A malformed cooldown file can be overwritten without warning after its entries are treated as empty.
findings.why: When JSON parses but deserializes to `null` entries or invalid entry data, or its version is unsupported, `ReadStrict` returns `Unreadable(...)` as an empty list. `Rewrite` then applies a park or lift and writes that list, replacing the existing file. For example, after an upgrade changes the version or a partial edit leaves valid JSON with an invalid entry, a later round silently discards every previously parked quota and may run exhausted models again.
findings.fix: Distinguish a missing file from an unreadable or unsupported file in the locked read. Refuse the mutation and preserve the original file whenever the existing file cannot be safely interpreted; only replace it through an explicit recovery path.
findings.reason: Same as finding 0: overwriting a torn or unsupported-version file whole is the plan's §8 rule (S19), with one warning logged; an I/O failure of the read is refused, not overwritten. A future version change is that version's migration to write, not this plan's.

findings.title: The store accepts arbitrary keys and reset values, allowing unbounded file growth and invalid cooldowns.
findings.why: `Park`/`Change` persist caller-supplied keys and `UntilUtc` without validation. If an unexpected model identifier repeatedly produces unique unknown-family keys, each refusal can add another entry; the stated ten-entry size check does not enforce the promised 16 KiB budget. A malformed or past reset can also be written and immediately stop excluding the row, while an extreme future reset can park it indefinitely.
findings.fix: Validate keys against the supported quota-key forms, cap the number of entries and serialized file size before writing, and require a valid future UTC reset; refuse the write with a notice when any bound is exceeded.
findings.reason: Outside the plan and already bounded: keys come from QuotaKeyOf's closed table (codex, claude, kimi, three agy groups, one antigravity/?<model> per model a person configures — plan §8 projects under ten), every write drops expired entries, and S20 pins the 16 KiB ceiling. Parks come only from QuotaCooldowns.AfterRoundAsync, whose reset is already forced future (ResetOfAsync). Validating the store against its own callers is a new feature the plan did not ask for.

findings.title: The quota probe reuses the refused launch's environment, including its credential, for a different command.
findings.why: When an agy model refuses, `RequestFor` copies the invocation request and replaces only argv and stdin. The `/quota` process therefore receives the review launch's full environment, including `ANTIGRAVITY_API_KEY` and any other prompt-specific variables. The current command may be trusted, but this unnecessarily sends credentials across a separate process invocation and makes them available to command-side tooling or diagnostics.
findings.fix: Build the probe environment from the minimum required agy configuration, explicitly excluding credentials and other launch-only variables unless `/quota` demonstrably requires them; keep secrets off argv and logs.
findings.reason: By design, in the plan (D6 and AgyQuotaProbe.RequestFor's doc): the probe is the owner's own command, `agy -p /quota`, run with the refused launch's executable, environment and working directory, because agy reads its sign-in from that environment and a probe without it answers 'not signed in' and decides nothing. It is the same binary and the same account, not a different recipient; the key is not in argv or logs (the launcher redacts both).

findings.title: Quota cooldown decision picks the first refusal instead of letting Spent: true or Spent: null dominate an answered launch across the quota key
findings.why: When multiple rows share the same quota key (e.g. two Gemini models in antigravity/gemini) and one succeeds while another hits a spent quota (RateLimited with Spent: true or spent by words), Refusal(rows) correctly identifies the refusal. However, in PlanAsync (line 349), if Refusal(rows) returns non-null, but for an undecided refusal GaugeDecides is true and the gauge returns GaugeAvailable or GaugeUnknown, PlanAsync falls back to calling Answers(key, rows). In the opposite scenario where Refusal(rows) evaluates rows, Refusal(rows) uses FirstWhere which returns the first matching item in arbitrary order without grouping/aggregation across multiple refusals; more critically, when an answered launch (Ok) happens in the same round, PlanAsync unconditionally runs the refusal branch if any refusal is found, even if an answer was newer or if answers and transient errors occur. But specifically when an undecided refusal probe returns GaugeAvailable, PlanAsync calls Answers(key, rows), producing a Lift plan if any sibling row succeeded. Conversely, if a key had one Ok launch and one transient refusal (GaugeAvailable) but no other rows, it will lift a standing cooldown for that key even though one row failed transiently. This breaks state stability when multiple invocations run under the same quota group.
findings.fix: Structure PlanAsync with an explicit state reducer over all rows in the group: evaluate whether any launch explicitly spent the quota first, then whether all launches succeeded or whether transient errors should leave existing cooldowns untouched rather than lifting or parking inappropriately.
findings.reason: Not a defect; the scenario described is the designed behaviour. A spent refusal wins over a sibling answer (Refusal first, Answers only when no refusal parks — S22/S23, documented on Answers). A transient refusal whose gauge says Available together with an Ok row of the same quota means the quota answered: lifting is exactly D4 ('an answered launch lifts it'). A standing cooldown is not reachable in that round anyway, since a cooling row is not launched.

findings.title: Probe failure during AfterRoundAsync falls back to QuotaReset.Guess without preserving the source or properly isolating failures
findings.why: In ResetOfAsync (line 390), if launcher is null, it falls back to QuotaReset.StatedOrGuess with Gauge = QuotaReset.GaugeUnknown, but if read throws OperationCanceledException in TryPlanAsync it catches it and drops the plan. However, when ReadResetAsync completes and untilUtc <= now (e.g., when the probe returns an expired reset time or stale bucket reset_time), ResetOfAsync forces a fallback via QuotaReset.Guess(reason, consecutive, now, reset.Note). This overrides the structured Source from 'quota' to 'guess' even if the probe was authoritative and meant to indicate the reset is past or immediate, thereby forcing an artificial doubling cooldown when the provider's gauge indicated expiration.
findings.fix: Handle an expired reset time from an authoritative gauge verdict by treating it as expired/available (or not parking), rather than mutating the reset into an artificial doubling guess cooldown.
findings.reason: Plan §S9-S14: a reset_time not after now is no reset, never a park on the past (AgyQuotaReport.ResetFor returns GroupMissing/CannotCheck for it); ResetOfAsync's `UntilUtc <= now` clause is the second guard against a parked-in-the-past entry, which would exclude nothing. A guess marked as such is the plan's answer when no usable reset exists.

findings.title: CanRun checks IsCooling but ReasonFor computes CoolingReasonOf after RowRefusal, masking auth status differences
findings.why: In PanelService.cs line 468, CanRun gates on !IsCooling(provider). In ReasonFor (line 543), CoolingReasonOf(provider) takes precedence over RuntimeResolution.ExclusionReason. In CoolingReasonOf (line 451), it checks AuthFor(provider).Auth != 'unavailable'. However, if a row is misconfigured (e.g. missing API key or invalid settings handled by ExclusionReason), but had a standing cooldown from a previous configuration or shared quota key, ReasonFor returns the cooling reason rather than the missing key / credential reason, masking actionable setup instructions from the operator until the cooldown expires.
findings.fix: Check credential/auth validity and specific exclusion reasons before returning CoolingReasonOf in ReasonFor.
findings.reason: Wrong: CoolingReasonOf already yields to the sign-in — its first condition is `AuthFor(provider).Auth != "unavailable"` (PanelService.cs:452), the very case the finding names; a row with a standing cooldown and a valid sign-in is reported as cooling, which is the point. Unknown model/other ExclusionReason cases are not reachable together with a standing quota key.

findings.title: AtomicFile.Write over FilePath creates a deadlocking file lock collision
findings.why: QuotaCooldowns.Rewrite is executed inside HeldFile.TakeWithin(LockPath, _lockWait), which takes and holds an exclusive FileShare.None lock on LockPath. But in QuotaCooldowns constructor, when lockWait or default parameters are initialized, FilePath is `quota-cooldowns.json` and LockPath is `quota-cooldowns.lock`. However, AtomicFile.Write uses a temporary sibling file and replaces/moves to FilePath. Crucially, in QuotaCooldowns.Rewrite, ReadStrict() reads FilePath while LockPath is locked. But if another process or thread uses HeldFile or AtomicFile without file locking directory synchronization, or when AtomicFile writes: look at AtomicFile.Write implementation in this repo. If LockPath was intended to protect FilePath, notice lines 189-204: ReadStrict() catches JsonException and calls Unreadable, but when File.ReadAllText throws IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException during ReadStrict called inside Rewrite (line 157: `var live = ReadStrict().Where(...)`), it is NOT caught by ReadStrict's handler (it only catches FileNotFoundException, DirectoryNotFoundException, and JsonException). That unhandled IOException escapes Rewrite into Change's catch block, which turns it into a CooldownWrite.Refused. However, more critically: in `Change`, if `AtomicFile.Write` throws or if a concurrent read occurs, look at line 149: `var live = ReadStrict().Where(entry => entry.UntilUtc > now).ToArray(); AfterLockedRead?.Invoke(); var next = change(live, now); if (next.SequenceEqual(live)) return new CooldownWrite.Unchanged(); AtomicFile.Write(FilePath, Serialize(next));`. Notice `next.SequenceEqual(live)`: `live` is a materialized array of `QuotaCooldownEntry` (records), and `next` is returned by `change`. For `Park` (line 114), `new QuotaCooldownEntry(key, untilUtc.ToUniversalTime(), source, model, kept, now, consecutive)`. Since `now` is evaluated once in `Rewrite` (line 148: `var now = Now;`) and passed to `change(live, now)`, if `Park` is called with an identical entry or consecutive count update, but in `Lift(string key)`: if `key` is not present, `next.SequenceEqual(live)` is true and returns Unchanged. BUT in `Apply` (line 387): `var kept = entries.Where(entry => !touched.Contains(entry.Key)); var parked = plans.Where(plan => plan.Park is not null).Select(plan => EntryOf(plan, entries, now)); return [.. kept, .. parked];`. Notice that `Apply` returns entries ordered by plan insertion order (kept first, then parked). But `live` in `Rewrite` was read from disk where `Serialize` ordered entries by Key (ordinal). Because `next` has entries in a different order (kept, then newly parked), `next.SequenceEqual(live)` compares elements positionally! If `next` contains the exact same elements as `live` but in different order or with re-added identical key, SequenceEqual fails and rewrites the file, but when compared to existing entries: if a round completes and decides no state change or an identical park, SequenceEqual fails due to element ordering, causing unnecessary locked disk churn every single round.
findings.fix: Sort `next` by Key ordinal before `next.SequenceEqual(live)` or compare sets/order-independent sequences.
findings.reason: Wrong. Nothing deadlocks: LockPath is a separate file from FilePath and AtomicFile.Write publishes by move. The SequenceEqual claim: a parked entry carries SinceUtc = now, so a re-park never equals the live list and is a real write; a lift of an absent key leaves `kept` in the live (file, Key-sorted) order and compares equal, which is the Unchanged case (tested). The IOException from ReadStrict is caught by Change and becomes a Refused, as the finding itself concedes.

findings.title: EntryOf in QuotaCooldowns.Apply passes park.Reset.Source instead of QuotaReset.FromGuess, resetting consecutive counter
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.EntryOf` (line 393): `var consecutive = ConsecutiveAfter(entries, plan.Key, park.Reset.Source);`. Looking at `ConsecutiveAfter` (line 230): `entries.FirstOrDefault(entry => entry.Key == key) is { Source: QuotaReset.FromGuess } previous && source == QuotaReset.FromGuess ? previous.Consecutive + 1 : 0;`. But when `ResetOfAsync` is called (line 369): if `reset.UntilUtc <= now`, it calls `QuotaReset.Guess(reason, consecutive, now, reset.Note)`. In other paths, e.g. `AgyQuotaVerdict.SpentWithoutReset`, `WithGauge` returns `QuotaReset.StatedOrGuess(reason, consecutive, nowUtc, note) with { Gauge = gauge }`. If `Stated` found no stated reset, `StatedOrGuess` returns `Guess`, whose `Source` is `QuotaReset.FromGuess` ("guess"). However, in `QuotaCooldowns.PlanAsync` (line 327), `reset` was already computed by `ResetOfAsync` using `var consecutive = NextConsecutive(key, now);` (line 363), where `consecutive` was calculated from the pre-round standing entry! Then in `EntryOf` inside `Apply`, it calls `ConsecutiveAfter(entries, plan.Key, park.Reset.Source)`. If the existing entry already had consecutive = 1, `NextConsecutive` passed 2 to `ReadResetAsync`/`Guess`. But `EntryOf` recalculates `consecutive` again using `ConsecutiveAfter(entries, plan.Key, park.Reset.Source)` which does `previous.Consecutive + 1`. If `previous` entry in `entries` has expired (`UntilUtc <= now`), `entries` in `Rewrite` was filtered: line 149 `var live = ReadStrict().Where(entry => entry.UntilUtc > now).ToArray();`. So `entries` passed to `Apply` ONLY contains non-expired entries! If the entry had expired before the round ran, `entries.FirstOrDefault(entry => entry.Key == key)` returns null, so `ConsecutiveAfter` evaluates to 0. Meanwhile, `park.Reset` was built with `Guess` using `consecutive` (from `NextConsecutive`, which also looked up `Standing` and got 0). But if the entry was STILL standing when the round started, `Reset` used `consecutive` = N+1 for fallback backoff calculation in `CooldownParser.Fallback(reason, consecutive)`. But if the entry expired during the round before `Rewrite` locked read, `CooldownParser.Fallback` used the old backoff, but stored `consecutive` becomes 0, creating a mismatch between stored `consecutive` and the actual `UntilUtc` interval.
findings.fix: Preserve the consecutive count computed when determining `park.Reset` rather than recalculating it against the filtered live entries.
findings.reason: By design: the reset is computed outside the lock with NextConsecutive from the standing entry, and the stored count is re-read from the LIVE list inside the lock so two processes agree (documented on EntryOf, S35). The two can differ only when the entry expires between the probe and the write, and then 'doubling restarts after a gap' is the documented rule (NextConsecutive).

findings.title: CoolingSentence crashes with OverflowException or formatting bugs if clock skew makes untilUtc earlier than nowUtc
findings.why: In `PanelService.LeftOf` (line 442): `var left = untilUtc - nowUtc; return left.TotalHours >= 1 ? $"{(long)Math.Ceiling(left.TotalHours)} h" : $"{(long)Math.Ceiling(left.TotalMinutes)} min";`. If `nowUtc` is slightly ahead of `untilUtc` (e.g. race condition between `IsCooling` check and `CoolingSentence` formatting when time reaches expiration), `left.TotalHours` or `TotalMinutes` is negative (e.g., `-0.1`). `Math.Ceiling(-0.1)` returns `-0.0`, resulting in `"-0 min"` or negative time rendered in user-facing UI and round exclusion strings handed to calling AIs. Furthermore, if `untilUtc` is far in the past or invalid, `(long)Math.Ceiling(...)` can produce negative or strange strings.
findings.fix: Clamp `left` to `TimeSpan.Zero` (e.g. `if (left < TimeSpan.Zero) left = TimeSpan.Zero;`) before formatting `LeftOf`.
findings.reason: Not reachable as described: CoolingReasonOf only formats an entry Standing(key) just returned (UntilUtc > now), and the clock is read again a few microseconds later; the worst case is 'in 0 min' (Math.Ceiling of a negative fraction casts to 0), never a negative duration. A clamp would be defensive code for a state that cannot be shown in a test.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation and memory allocation when parsing large stderr in AgyError.Parse
findings.why: In `AgyError.Parse` (line 26): for every line starting with `AGY_ERROR`, it executes `var rest = line[Marker.Length..] + "\n" + string.Join('\n', lines[(i + 1)..]);`. If stderr contains many lines or multiple `AGY_ERROR` lines, slicing `lines[(i + 1)..]` and `string.Join` allocates full sub-arrays and re-concatenates the remaining stderr repeatedly for each error marker, causing quadratic allocation and memory pressure on unbounded stderr.
findings.fix: Find the line index and calculate substrings or read slices over memory/spans without rejoining all remaining lines repeatedly.
findings.reason: Not a defect at this scale: stderr is redacted and bounded by the executor before any adapter sees it, and an AGY_ERROR line occurs once or twice per refusal; the pretty-printed shape the plan requires (D2) needs the rest of stderr after the marker. A performance rewrite with no measured problem is outside the plan.

findings.title: RateLimited in ClaudeRuntime fails to parse valid JSON with trailing non-JSON output
findings.why: In `ClaudeRuntime.RateLimited` (line 178): `using var document = JsonDocument.Parse(result.StdOut.Trim());`. If Claude CLI prints any warning or trailing text before or after its JSON envelope (which Claude CLI frequently does on stderr or stdout during failures), `JsonDocument.Parse` throws `JsonException`. While this is caught, it falls back to `RateLimitVerdict.ByText(result)`, which skips structured spent classification (`Spent: true`), failing to recognize the monthly spend limit if envelope parsing fails.
findings.fix: Use a resilient JSON reader or extract the JSON envelope substring similar to how `AgyError` searches for JSON objects.
findings.reason: Outside the plan: ClaudeRuntime.RateLimited reads the CLI's JSON envelope (measured 2026-09-29); any other text, including a non-JSON line around it, is answered by the text exactly as before (documented in its remarks) — the unchanged behaviour. No observed Claude output has trailing non-JSON on a spend-limit failure, and the plan does not ask for a tolerant reader.

findings.title: Round completion blocks for up to 30 to 60 seconds awaiting sequential `/quota` subprocess probes without progress reporting
findings.why: In `RoundEngine.cs` at line 439, after all reviewers finish executing in `RunAllAsync`, the engine awaits `_cooldowns.AfterRoundAsync(results, cancellation.Token)` before returning the round results or summary. For any Antigravity launch that encounters a quota refusal, `PlanAllAsync` sequentially iterates through quota keys and runs `AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync`, which spawns `agy -p /quota` with a 30-second timeout (`AgyQuotaProbe.Timeout`). If one or more models hit quota, the caller experiences a silent freeze of 20 to 60 seconds after the review work is already finished; no progress notice or intermediate round status is sent to inform the user or UI that the server is waiting on external quota gauge queries.
findings.fix: Emit an in-flight progress notice before probing vendor gauges so the client UI shows that quota status is being verified, and query distinct quota keys concurrently with `Task.WhenAll` instead of awaiting them sequentially in a `foreach` loop.
findings.reason: Outside the plan (§8: 'one agy child per spent key per round, bounded at 30 s ... No cache, no retry'). At most three agy keys exist, a probe happens only after a spent agy refusal, and running them concurrently or adding a progress notice is a feature the plan did not specify; the engine's round result is unchanged either way.

findings.title: `Standing(key)` re-reads and parses `quota-cooldowns.json` synchronously from disk on every invocation, causing N+1 disk I/O on the 10-second polling path
findings.why: In `PanelService.cs` (`CoolingOf`, `CanRun`, and `CoolingReasonOf`), checking each provider's status invokes `_cooldowns.Standing(key)`. `Standing` executes `ReadEntries() -> ReadStrict()`, which performs synchronous `File.ReadAllText(FilePath)` and `JsonSerializer.Deserialize` without in-memory caching. The extension queries `ProbeAsync`/`ProvidersAsync` every 10 seconds; with 15 configured provider rows, this triggers 30 to 45 synchronous disk reads and JSON deserializations on the MCP server stdio thread on every poll cycle. At 10x input (e.g. 50+ model configurations in team settings), this creates hundreds of redundant disk operations every 10 seconds for a file that changes only when a quota resets.
findings.fix: Cache the parsed cooldown entries in memory in `QuotaCooldowns` (invalidated when `Change` writes or when the file modification time changes), or read the entries once per `ProbeAsync`/round pass rather than re-reading the filesystem inside `Standing`.
findings.reason: By design: D4 and the class summary say every decision reads the file, so a park by another coai-mcp process on the same data directory is seen on the next decision (§8: 'read the file on every decision'). A cache would hide it. The file is under 16 KiB and a read is one small ReadAllText; no measurement shows a cost.

findings.title: `ClaudeRuntime.RateLimited` parses full stdout JSON before checking `result.ExitCode != 0`, redundantly parsing successful review payloads
findings.why: In `ReviewerExecutor.cs` (line 1013), `invocation.Adapter?.RateLimited(invocation, result)` is called on every launch outcome, including successful reviews (`result.ExitCode == 0`). `ClaudeRuntime.RateLimited` immediately allocates and parses `result.StdOut.Trim()` with `JsonDocument.Parse` at line 177 before evaluating `result.ExitCode != 0`. On successful Claude reviews with large outputs (tens to hundreds of KiB of review findings), this forces a full DOM JSON parse and discard, only for `ReviewerExecutor` to parse stdout a second time immediately afterwards.
findings.fix: Return `RateLimitVerdict.ByText(result)` immediately at the start of `ClaudeRuntime.RateLimited` if `result.ExitCode == 0`, avoiding unnecessary JSON parsing on all successful reviewer launches.
findings.reason: No behaviour changes: the executor parses the same stdout again for the envelope, and parse-first-then-exit-code is the order whose result is identical for exit 0 (ByText). A micro-optimisation without a measured cost, outside the plan's scope.

findings.title: §6 and §7 do not require a live check of the server-to-extension cooldown contract
findings.why: S38 checks that the server serializes a hand-built `ProvidersAnswer`, while S30 feeds a separately hand-built object to the extension parser. If the actual server response changes shape or field names, both tests can pass while the extension silently omits the cooldown and users see a cooling model as runnable.
findings.fix: Add and run one scenario that obtains the real `--providers` response with a cooldown and passes it through the extension parser or running page; assert that the card shows the cooldown.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: §8's 30-second lock wait can delay delivery of completed round results
findings.why: `RoundEngine` awaits `AfterRoundAsync` before producing the summary, and D4 allows its lock acquisition to wait 30 seconds. If another process holds the lock for that interval, reviews are already complete but the caller still waits up to 30 seconds for their results, contrary to D4's claim that a refused write does not delay completed results.
findings.fix: Specify a lock wait bound that does not materially delay result delivery, or arrange for summary delivery to proceed independently of the cooldown write.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D4 fixes the 30 s lock wait on purpose, plan gate round 2 F5.)

findings.title: Section 3 (D4, D5, D9) & Section 7: Active cooldowns can never be lifted by an answered launch because CanRun excludes the row from ever running
findings.why: Concrete situation: An Antigravity Gemini model hits a weekly quota limit. D4 and D5 park `antigravity/gemini` with `untilUtc` set 63 hours in the future. The user upgrades their subscription or authenticates with a different account (`agy auth login`) and triggers a new review round. Outcome: `PanelService.CanRun` evaluates `!IsCooling(provider)`. Because `untilUtc > now`, `IsCooling` is true, causing `CanRun` to return false. `RosterBuilder.BuildWork` excludes the provider from the round roster entirely. The provider is never launched, never generates an `Ok` outcome, and `AfterRoundAsync` never executes `Lift(key)`. With manual unparking deferred as out of scope (D12) and file state surviving process restarts (S17), the user remains locked out for 63 hours despite having a working account, directly contradicting D4's claim that 'the note's worry (a re-login under a parked row) is answered by the lift'.
findings.fix: Provide an escape hatch in CanRun (or an explicit probe refresh / credentials check / manual unpark action) allowing a cooling row to attempt execution or query `/quota` on user demand rather than excluding it unconditionally until expiry.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D12 puts a manual try-now out of scope and the cooldown ends by itself at untilUtc; this is the plan's recorded decision, not a code defect.)

findings.title: Section 3 (D5) & Section 4 (S21, S39): Exponential backoff doubling for unknown reset times can never advance past 30 minutes in production
findings.why: Concrete situation: A model with an unstated reset time (such as Claude's monthly spend limit) fails. D5 parks the key with `source = guess` for 30 minutes with `consecutive = 0`. During these 30 minutes, `CanRun` excludes the model from all rounds, so no launches or failures can occur. At minute 31, the 30-minute window has expired. The next round runs, launches the model, and it fails again because the spend limit has not reset. D5 and S39 dictate that 'Doubling restarts after expiry... an expired entry is deleted (D4), so a refusal after a gap starts at 30 minutes again'. Because the expired entry is purged before or during the write, `consecutive` is reset to 0, and the new cooldown is set to 30 minutes again. Outcome: The 30-minute doubling ladder (30m -> 60m -> 120m -> 240m -> 5h in S21) can never reach step 1 or beyond in real execution; the model retries and fails every 30 minutes indefinitely without exponential backoff.
findings.fix: Track and retain `consecutive` failure counts across expired cooldowns (e.g. using a separate 24-hour retention window before resetting `consecutive` to 0) rather than resetting the count immediately upon `untilUtc` expiry.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D5 and S39 decide that doubling restarts after expiry.)

findings.title: Section 3 (D5) & Section 4 (S18, S25): Unit tests directly invoke AfterRoundAsync and Lift with mocked outcomes, masking the unreachable lift path
findings.why: Concrete situation: The DoD guarantees that 'an answered launch lifts it (S18, S25)'. S18 tests `Lift(key)` directly on `QuotaCooldowns`, while S25 supplies a synthesized `Ok` outcome directly into `AfterRoundAsync(results, ct)`. Outcome: The test suite passes green, but no test exercises `RoundEngine.RunAllAsync` or `PanelService.CanRun` in conjunction with `AfterRoundAsync`. This creates the false impression that active cooldowns are self-healing upon successful round execution, while in the running application `CanRun` prevents any `Ok` outcome from ever being generated while cooling down.
findings.fix: Add an integrated test verifying round execution against a cooling provider to prove whether and how an account can actually achieve recovery and trigger a lift.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The code has an engine-level test, ARoundThatEndsSpentParksTheQuotaTests, for the park road.)

findings.title: Section 3 (D8) & Section 4 (S31): Date formatting specification produces slashes instead of dots under the en-GB locale
findings.why: Concrete situation: S31 and D9 require formatting timestamps as `dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm` (e.g. `14.10.2026 09:19`). D8 specifies using `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { day, month, year, hour, minute, hourCycle: 'h23', timeZone? })`. Outcome: In standard JavaScript/V8 engines, the `en-GB` locale formats date components with forward slashes (e.g. `14/10/2026, 09:19`), not dots. The assertion in S31 expecting `14.10.2026 09:19` will fail strict equality against the output of the specified `Intl.DateTimeFormat` call.
findings.fix: Explicitly specify delimiter replacement (e.g. `.replace(/\//g, '.')` and removing commas) or use custom date formatting helper tokens to produce the dotted format reliably across runtimes.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. No code defect either: cooldownWords.dateTimeOf builds the text from formatToParts joined with dots, not from the en-GB literal.

findings.title: Quota keys and cooldown sources travel through business logic as untyped strings
findings.why: The C# doctrine says, “A business concept does not travel as a `string` or an `int. Wrap it in a typed value with parsing and validation.” `QuotaKeyOf` returns `string`, and the cooldown record and reset also carry keys and sources as strings, so invalid or mismatched values can pass through the storage and service boundaries unchecked. The plan specifies string values in the persisted record (`key` and `source`), but that does not require untyped strings in business logic.
findings.fix: Introduce typed quota-key and cooldown-source values for runtime and service boundaries, with source-generated JSON serialization preserving the required string fields in `quota-cooldowns.json`.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope: D3 fixes the interface as `string QuotaKeyOf(string model)` and the persisted record as string key/source (QuotaSources constants name the values). A typed-value redesign of the runtime interface is a plan change; the plan is frozen for this change.

findings.title: Valid but malformed cooldown entries can park a quota indefinitely.
findings.why: If the cooldown file contains valid JSON with a matching key and a far-future `untilUtc`—for example after a mistaken manual edit—the parser accepts it without checking the key, source, timestamp range, or note. `Standing` then excludes every row sharing that quota until the supplied instant, potentially year 9999, with no warning that the file is malformed.
findings.fix: Validate each entry against the known quota-key and source formats and a reasonable timestamp bound; treat invalid entries as an unreadable file or discard them with a warning.
findings.reason: Not a defect of this change: the file is coai's own state in the user's data directory and only the writer produces entries (bounded by CooldownParser.MaxStatedWait / the gauge reset). A hand-written far-future entry is a deliberate park by whoever edited the file, and the plan asks for no bound or schema check beyond fail-open on an unreadable file (D4). Deleting the file lifts it.

findings.title: Quota probes run serially before the round can return its results.
findings.why: If spent outcomes cover Gemini, Argon, and the Claude/GPT quota groups, each `/quota` probe can take up to 30 seconds. `DecideAsync` awaits each group in sequence, and `RoundEngine` awaits `AfterRoundAsync` before producing the summary, so users can wait up to 90 extra seconds after reviews finish without a progress update.
findings.fix: Run independent per-key probes concurrently, then apply their aggregate changes in one locked write; keep the probes bounded by the existing timeout.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope and not a defect: D5 specifies one /quota call per spent key, bounded at 30 s by the launcher; it does not ask for concurrency. The worst case needs all three agy groups spent in one round AND each probe to hit its timeout; a probe normally answers in seconds, and agy probes share one sign-in, so running them concurrently is not obviously safer.

findings.title: PanelService resolves quota keys via new ephemeral runtime instances rather than runtime registrations
findings.why: Calling `RuntimeFor(provider)?.QuotaKeyOf(...)` inside `Cooling` calls `RuntimeResolution.For(provider.Identity())`, which instantiates a brand new runtime object on every check. While currently mostly stateless, this bypasses the registered runtime service pipeline and duplicates adapter instantiation logic. More critically, `QuotaRound.DecideAsync` obtains the key via `r.Invocation.Adapter?.QuotaKeyOf(...)`.
