If custom runtime configurations, dynamic model overrides, or runtime state/options are added in the future, `PanelService.Cooling` and `QuotaRound.DecideAsync` will diverge on how keys are derived.
findings.fix: Pass the active runtime instances or extract `QuotaKeyOf` into a dedicated quota key mapping strategy/service shared by both `PanelService` and runtime adapters, avoiding ephemeral instantiations.
findings.reason: Wrong: RuntimeResolution.For is the existing pattern (PanelService.RuntimeFor is already used at PanelService.cs:141, :314, :315, :353 for card warnings, survivor marker and the fast tier), the runtimes are stateless, and QuotaRound uses the invocation's adapter, which comes from the same RuntimeResolution.For. D9 prescribes `RuntimeFor(provider)?.QuotaKeyOf(provider.Model)`. No divergence exists today.

findings.title: Uncached lock-free disk reads in QuotaCooldowns.Standing hit the filesystem repeatedly per provider per check
findings.why: Every invocation of `CanRun`, `ExcludedFrom`, `ProvidersAsync`, and UI probes reads and deserializes `quota-cooldowns.json` directly from disk (`Standing` -> `ReadFile()`). In a round evaluating multiple providers across multiple stages, or during high-frequency provider polls, this performs redundant file I/O and JSON parsing for every row. As provider counts or probe frequencies increase, this disk thrashing adds unnecessary latency.
findings.fix: Maintain an in-memory cached snapshot of the parsed cooldown entries invalidating on file write or via timestamp/file-watcher check, falling back to disk read only when modified.
findings.reason: Decided by the plan: D4 says 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever, section 8)'. A cache would also hide another process's park/lift, which D4 and the cross-process section rely on (a park by one process is seen by the others on their next round).

findings.title: Model family parsing uses string stripping for fixed suffixes instead of regex or structured tokens
findings.why: In `AgyQuotaGroups.Family`, checking `model.EndsWith(effort)` only strips specific hardcoded suffixes `-low`, `-medium`, `-high`. If new effort levels or model tags are introduced (e.g. `-preview`, `-thinking`, `-mini`), the family lookup fails silently and classifies known models into the un-gauged `antigravity/?<model>` fallback, breaking quota monitoring for those models.
findings.fix: Define a structured model name parser or regex matching recognized vendor family patterns rather than stripping a hardcoded array of effort suffixes.
findings.reason: Decided by the plan: D3 requires 'one explicit, measured table' and says an unknown family gets its own key with no inferred group (a prefix or pattern rule would have parked every Gemini row when only Argon is spent). Adding a family is one table row with the fixture that shows it.

findings.title: Null elements in the cooldowns file cause an unhandled NullReferenceException that escapes ReadFile and breaks provider checks
findings.why: If quota-cooldowns.json contains a null element in the 'entries' array (e.g. '{"v":1,"entries":[null]}'), 'file.Entries.Where(e => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(e.Key)...)' dereferences 'e.Key' on a null item. The resulting NullReferenceException is not caught by 'ReadFile' (which catches only JsonException, IOException, and UnauthorizedAccessException), violating Doctrine 4a and the plan requirement that an unreadable file fails open. The unhandled exception propagates through 'Standing' into 'CanRun', 'ProvidersAsync', and round execution.
findings.fix: Add a null guard in the filter predicate ('e is not null && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(e.Key) && e.UntilUtc != default') and catch NullReferenceException alongside JsonException in ReadFile to safely fail open.
findings.reason: Confirmed by test: `{"v":1,"entries":[null]}` deserializes a null element and `e.Key` throws NullReferenceException out of Standing, through CanRun; D4 requires every unreadable file to fail open. Fixed with a null guard; test ANullEntryInTheFile_IsSkipped_AndItsSiblingsStillStand.

findings.title: Exception filter on probe cancellation causes an unhandled OperationCanceledException that aborts quota processing for all other keys
findings.why: In DecideKeyAsync, ParkedAsync is wrapped in 'catch (OperationCanceledException) when (ct.IsCancellationRequested)'. When AgyQuotaProbe runs and returns result.Cancelled == true (for instance, if the process launcher cancels or kills the probe process tree independently), Judged throws a new OperationCanceledException without ct.IsCancellationRequested being true. Because of the filter, the exception escapes DecideKeyAsync and bubbles to AfterRoundAsync, aborting the DecideAsync loop and discarding quota updates (both parks and lifts) for all subsequent provider keys in the round.
findings.fix: Remove the 'when (ct.IsCancellationRequested)' filter so that any OperationCanceledException during a key's probe is caught for that key, ensuring sibling keys continue to be processed as stated in the method's own contract.
findings.reason: Cannot happen with the real launcher: ProcessResult.Cancelled is set only as `timedOut && ct.IsCancellationRequested` (ProcessLauncher.cs:527,570), and AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync calls ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() before Judged, so any OperationCanceledException from the probe has ct cancelled and the filter matches. The filter was added on purpose in the first review's R2 fix.

findings.title: PanelService re-reads and parses quota-cooldowns.json from disk per provider on multiple roster and status query paths
findings.why: Cooling(provider) calls _cooldowns.Standing(key, now), which invokes ReadFile() -> File.ReadAllText(FilePath) + JsonSerializer.Deserialize on every call without caching. In CanRun(provider), ReasonFor(provider), and ProvidersAsync(), every provider evaluated triggers a separate synchronous disk read and JSON parse. For a configuration with 10–20 providers or during round roster building across stages, a single status query or roster evaluation performs dozens of redundant synchronous disk I/O operations.
findings.fix: Cache the parsed QuotaCooldownFile in-memory with a short TTL or invalidate on file write/file mtime check, or read once per ProvidersAsync/BuildWork pass and evaluate providers against the in-memory snapshot.
findings.reason: Duplicate of the uncached-read finding (index 4): D4 decides 'no cache'.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse allocates split arrays and parses JSON documents for every line in launch stderr
findings.why:
On failed reviewer launches where stderr contains verbose logs or stack traces (e.g. hundreds or thousands of lines), stderr.Split('
', ...) allocates an array of strings for all lines. For each line starting with AGY_ERROR, JsonDocument.Parse is called. If agy dumps large stderr payloads, splitting the entire string into substrings allocates significant heap memory on the error handling path.
findings.fix: Use a line reader or MemoryExtensions.EnumerateLines(stderr.AsSpan()) to iterate stderr lines without allocating string arrays, and only allocate or parse JSON when the line prefix matches AGY_ERROR.
findings.reason: Not a defect: the launcher bounds the captured stderr (BoundedText) and the failed-launch path runs once per launch, so the split is a bounded, one-off allocation on an error path; no scenario of the plan or its definition of done is affected.

findings.title: TimeLeft displays '0 min' or misleading negative bounds if nowUtc exceeds UntilUtc before expiry check
findings.why: CooldownWords.TimeLeft computes left = entry.UntilUtc - nowUtc and formats with Math.Max(1, Math.Ceiling(left.TotalMinutes)). If nowUtc has passed untilUtc slightly before Standing drops the entry or during clock skew/formatting race, left is negative or zero, yet Math.Max(1, Math.Ceiling(negative)) can return 1 min instead of indicating readiness or empty remaining duration.
findings.fix: Guard against left <= TimeSpan.Zero in TimeLeft or Sentence by returning empty or stating that the reset time has elapsed.
findings.reason: Not a defect: Standing returns only entries whose end lies after the clock, so TimeLeft sees a positive span except across a few microseconds between two clock reads; Math.Max(1, ...) is deliberate (rounded UP, so a person is never told a quota is back before it is), the same rule as the card's spanOf.

findings.title: §4/S42 and §7 claim cancellation leaves the round results intact, but the plan has no check that verifies results reach the round summary
findings.why: When the round token is cancelled during `/quota`, S42 checks only that `AfterRoundAsync` returns its input list unchanged. That does not prove `RoundEngine` continues to `:443` and publishes the completed results; an exception or cancellation path in the engine could still discard them while this scenario passes.
findings.fix: Add a scenario through `RoundEngine` that cancels the probe after reviewer results complete and asserts the completed results still appear in the summary.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Noted for the code round: whether RoundEngine publishes completed results when the probe is cancelled.)

findings.title: §3/D4 fail-open handling treats a missing cooldown file as a read failure and can hide a valid existing park
findings.why: On a first run, the file is absent, which is normal; after a park, if the file is temporarily unreadable or disappears, the specified fail-open behavior lets the row run. If the next write then replaces the unreadable state, a previously persisted cooldown can be lost, so the same spent quota is called again despite the plan promising restart persistence and cross-process visibility.
findings.fix: Distinguish an expected missing file from corruption and transient I/O failures; specify and test the behavior for unreadable existing data, including whether a later write may overwrite it.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The code already distinguishes a missing file from an unreadable one: commit ebbf6b30, ACooldownFileThatCannotBeReadIsNotReplacedTests.)

findings.title: §7 says every listed scenario is observed red first, while §12 records scenarios whose required red-first evidence is absent
findings.why: The DoD requires S1–S43 each to be seen red first, but §12 says the story 2–4 implementations were written before their tests, and that S3, S6, and S8 break-it variants were not run. The team cannot use the stated completion criterion to determine whether the required red-first checks happened.
findings.fix: Correct the DoD to match the recorded evidence, and name any remaining required red-first or break-it runs as outstanding work.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: D5 / S41 parks an explicitly spent row on stale error text when the gauge reports Available, creating an indefinite ungrounded cooldown loop
findings.why: In D5 and S41, when an agy launch returns Spent == true, but the post-round /quota probe reports Available, the plan dictates parking on stated or guess anyway under the premise that 'the refusal is the newer fact'. If agy emits a false or transient 'Individual quota reached' error (or if quota immediately replenished/reset between the launch and the post-round probe), the model is parked for up to 88+ hours (stated) based on text that the authoritative /quota API explicitly contradicts. Because the model is excluded from rounds while cooling down, it is never launched again until expiry; upon expiry, if it fails once more, the same cycle repeats, locking out a working account without verifying whether the quota is actually spent.
findings.fix: In D5, when the /quota probe executes successfully and reports Available for the target bucket, treat the gauge as authoritative over the refusal text (or park only for a short grace interval, e.g. 5 minutes, rather than the multi-day stated reset) and log the disparity as an unverified exhaustion instead of parking for 88h.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D5/S41 deliberately takes the refusal as the newer fact; that is a recorded design decision of the plan.)

findings.title: D5 / D12 omits consultation, question-row, and consultant-check rounds from cooldown tracking despite sharing the same agy CLI quota
findings.why: Section D12 explicitly excludes consultation turns, consultant checks, and question rows from AfterRoundAsync and CanRun. In concrete terms, if an agy quota is exhausted during a code or plan round, a subsequent consultation or consultant-check launch will still invoke the spent agy CLI model, suffering the exact 10-30 minute launch timeouts that #878 was logged to prevent. Conversely, if a consultation exhausts the agy quota, it writes resetsUtc to the ledger but does not trigger AfterRoundAsync, so the next review round launches the spent CLI anyway.
findings.fix: Clarify that consultation and question-row roads must either check Standing(key, now) before launch or record the cooldown via QuotaCooldowns upon quota failure, or document the unhandled timeout risk explicitly as a known limitation in the symptom description.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D12 names consultation turns as out of scope on purpose.)

findings.title: D9 / S31 cooldown line displays empty string immediately when untilUtc passes while the row remains excluded until the next probe refresh
findings.why: When nowMs >= untilUtc, cooldownLine returns '' (an empty string). However, PanelService.ProbeAsync is polled on a 10s interval by the webview panel. For up to 10 seconds after an entry expires, the model card will render with an empty cooldown line while still being treated as cooling down or excluded in the backend until the next probe cycle updates the status, leading to UI flicker or a blank badge/line.
findings.fix: Have cooldownLine return an explicit transitional status such as 'cooldown expired — refreshing' when untilUtc is passed, or ensure the badge and line clear atomically based on the same state.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: Stories 2–4 were implemented before their tests were written.
findings.why: The plan says the real implementation was written before the test files for stories 2–4. This breaks the rule: “The order is fixed — never fix first and test after.” The later stub-based red runs do not establish that the tests first reproduced the real defect before the fix.
findings.fix: For each affected story, revert the production behavior, write and run its regression test until it fails for the real symptom, then restore the implementation and confirm the test passes.
findings.reason: Process finding about history, not a defect in the code. The plan's §12 already records that stories 2-4 were coded before their tests; each scenario was then run red against a stub of the production code (reds are recorded in the coder notes) and the first review's fixes (R1-R6) were all test-first. Re-ordering done work cannot be fixed in a commit and the tests do fail for the stated reasons.

findings.title: The changed server-to-extension contract is not reflected in the architecture overview.
findings.why: The new `cooldown` wire field changes interaction between `src_mcp` and `src_vs_code`, but this diff updates module docs without updating `research/architecture.md`. The rule says: “If cross-module or cross-repository interaction changed — update `research/architecture.md` too.”
findings.fix: Update `research/architecture.md` to describe the cooldown field and the server-extension interaction, and re-render any affected Mermaid diagrams.
findings.reason: Right: architecture.md documents the --providers members, and the new optional `cooldown` member crosses src_mcp and src_vs_code. Added a section to research/architecture.md (commit 4a045a85).

findings.title: The required nullable spent verdict conflicts with the C# doctrine's ban on null in business logic.
findings.why: `Spent` is a business verdict represented as `bool?`, while the doctrine says: “No null in business logic” and allows nullables only for named cases that do not include tri-state verdicts. The plan requires `RateLimitVerdict and ReviewerOutcome.RateLimited carry a three-valued bool? Spent`. These requirements conflict, so this implementation cannot satisfy both as written.
findings.fix: Reconcile the doctrine with the plan by explicitly allowing this tri-state verdict, or revise the plan and use a non-null typed three-state value.
findings.reason: The plan mandates it: D1 fixes `bool? Spent` three-valued on RateLimitVerdict and RateLimited (true/false/null = nobody said), and the plan is frozen for this change. The null here is the tri-state's third value, documented at the member, not an absent business object.

findings.title: An unreadable or malformed cooldown file is silently treated as empty during a locked write
findings.why: If the cooldown file is malformed JSON or exceeds the size limit, `ReadEntries(underLock: true)` routes it through `Unreadable` and returns no entries; `Locked` then writes the new change over it. Any valid cooldowns already in that file are lost, contrary to the required refusal to overwrite a bad or unreadable file. The read-error catch avoids this for I/O and access failures, but not for parse failures or an oversized file.
findings.fix: Make `ReadEntries` return a distinct invalid/unreadable result under the lock for every malformed, oversized, or unreadable file, and have `Locked` refuse the write without replacing it.
findings.reason: Opened the code: a file that is torn/unparseable (JsonException), not version 1, or over the size guard is deliberately read as no cooldown with one warning and 'is overwritten whole by the next park' - plan §8 and S19 say exactly that, and an unparseable file holds no recoverable park. What must NOT be overwritten is a file that is merely unreadable right now (I/O, permissions): that already propagates under the lock and Locked refuses (commit ebbf6b30, ACooldownFileThatCannotBeReadIsNotReplacedTests). The finding asks for the opposite of the plan's S19.

findings.title: A single non-cancelled quota probe can block round completion for up to 30 seconds per spent key
findings.why: AfterRoundAsync awaits ReadResetAsync once for each distinct spent key, and AgyQuotaProbe gives each CLI call a 30-second timeout. If six agy quota groups or rows are spent and each `/quota` call times out, the finished round waits for as much as three minutes before its summary is built; the other reviewers have already finished, but the caller sees no completed result during that wait.
findings.fix: Bound the total post-round probe budget, or make each key's probe budget substantially shorter and stop probing when the shared post-round budget expires; retain already-decided changes when that budget ends.
findings.reason: Within the plan's stated budget: §8 'The probe' - one agy child per spent key per round, bounded at 30 s by the launcher; the keys are three agy families plus rare unknown models, and only a spent key is probed. Bounding the sum or parallelising is an enhancement the plan did not ask for and would change the one-gauge-call-per-key sequencing; out of scope.

findings.title: The file-size guard accepts files sixteen times larger than the documented 16 KiB budget
findings.why: If a malformed or externally enlarged cooldown file is 20 KiB, ReadEntries still deserializes it and treats its entries as usable; the stated under-16-KiB bound is therefore not enforced on reads, and repeated reads parse up to 256 KiB on every roster/card decision.
findings.fix: Set MostBytes below 16 KiB and reject any file at or above that limit.
findings.reason: The 16 KiB figure is the budget of what this code WRITES (proved by S20); the 256 KiB read guard only keeps a foreign or runaway file from being read into memory, and a hand-enlarged file with valid entries is still correct data. Not a defect against the plan.

findings.title: QuotaCooldowns uses synchronous file I/O inside Task.Run while RoundEngine awaits it, violating non-blocking async architecture
findings.why: In QuotaCooldowns.AfterRoundAsync, `await Task.Run(() => Apply(changes), CancellationToken.None)` is called. Inside `Apply`, `HeldFile.TakeWithin` and `Locked` perform blocking synchronous file I/O (`File.ReadAllText`, `AtomicFile.Write`) and spinning thread sleeps (`Thread.Sleep`) under a 30-second lock timeout. When multiple rounds or processes contend for `quota-cooldowns.lock`, threadpool threads are blocked synchronously for up to 30 seconds rather than yielding asynchronously, violating family async doctrine and coupling RoundEngine to blocking I/O.
findings.fix: Use async file operations (`File.ReadAllTextAsync`, `AtomicFile.WriteAsync`) and an asynchronous lock acquisition seam (`HeldFile.TakeWithinAsync`) with `await Task.Delay` instead of `Thread.Sleep`, or execute the file persistence in a dedicated decoupled queue without blocking worker threads.
findings.reason: Already covered: the first review's R4 moved Apply onto Task.Run precisely so the blocking lock spin never holds the round's continuation (common.reliability; ConsultantPlaces does the same). HeldFile/AtomicFile have only the synchronous API in this repository; writing async twins for a file of a few hundred bytes is outside the plan's scope.

findings.title: AntigravityRuntime violates abstraction boundaries by invoking CLI probes directly inside adapter contract
findings.why: IReviewerRuntime.ReadResetAsync passes `IProcessLauncher` directly into `AntigravityRuntime`, which then executes an external CLI command (`agy -p /quota ...`) via `AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync`. Runtimes are review execution adapters, not probe orchestration services. Entangling external CLI process execution into `IReviewerRuntime.ReadResetAsync` couples the reviewer abstraction to process launching and makes testing or mocking quota checks require faking general process launcher invocations rather than having a dedicated `IQuotaGauge` or `IAgyQuotaService` abstraction.
findings.fix: Extract quota probe discovery into a separate probe abstraction (e.g. `IAgyQuotaProbe` or `IQuotaResetReader`) that can be injected into `QuotaCooldowns` or the adapter, separating runner execution logic from gauge probing.
findings.reason: The plan's D3/D6 decision: IReviewerRuntime.ReadResetAsync is the seam, the adapter reads its own vendor's gauge through the launcher the caller passes, and tests fake that launcher (AgyQuotaProbe is exercised that way in S9-S15, S42). A separate IQuotaGauge abstraction is a redesign of a frozen plan.

findings.title: CooldownReport record lacks explicit source generation registration in Native-AOT context
findings.why: ServerJsonContext relies on System.Text.Json source generators for Native-AOT compilation. `CooldownReport` is referenced as a property on `ProviderStatus`, which is registered, but standalone serialization or deserialization without explicit registration in source generation contexts can trigger reflection fallback or trimming issues if used outside `ProviderStatus` serialization contexts.
findings.fix: Add `[JsonSerializable(typeof(CooldownReport))]` to `ServerJsonContext` to ensure Native-AOT serialization compatibility remains explicit and consistent with sibling DTOs.
findings.reason: Wrong: CooldownReport is a property type of ProviderStatus, which the source generator already covers transitively; its sibling SurvivorMarkerReport (also a nested property type) has no separate JsonSerializable either, and nothing serialises CooldownReport standalone.

findings.title: Auth check outranks cooling check in ExcludedFrom reason resolution
findings.why: In PanelService.cs lines 498-502, `CanRun` excludes a cooling row via `Cooling(provider) is null`. However, `ExcludedFrom` generates the exclusion reason: if `AuthFor(provider).Auth == "unavailable"` (e.g. key missing or expired), but the row also has a standing cooldown, or vice-versa, the check order `AuthFor(provider).Auth != "unavailable" && Cooling(provider) is { } cooling` means when Auth is unavailable, it falls through to `RuntimeResolution.ExclusionReason`. More critically, if a provider has `RowRefusal(provider).Length > 0` (such as prompt cap exceeded or effort unsupported), it reports `refused` rather than the cooldown, but if `Auth` check fails while cooling, it outputs an auth error. Furthermore, if a provider's model is parked on a quota cooldown, but `AuthFor` returns `unavailable`, `CanRun` is false, and `ExcludedFrom` reports an auth exclusion message rather than the cooldown message required by DoD 5 ('A cooling row is EXCLUDED from every stage's roster (and the security roster) by PanelService/RoundEngine with a sentence naming the return time in UTC').
findings.fix: Check `Cooling(provider)` before checking `AuthFor(provider)` in `ExcludedFrom`, or ensure `Cooling(provider) is { } cooling` produces `QuotaWords.Why(cooling, _clock.GetUtcNow())` whenever the provider is cooling down.
findings.reason: Deliberate and consistent with the sibling refusals: a row whose sign-in is unavailable (or that has a row refusal) cannot run whatever the clock says, and its auth/refusal sentence is the cure a person can act on, while a cooldown ends by itself. ExcludedFrom names a cooling row with the cooling sentence whenever the row is otherwise runnable (S26/S28). The plan's DoD 5 is about a cooling row, not about one that is also unable to sign in.

findings.title: AfterRoundAsync applies updates to QuotaCooldowns using CancellationToken.None on background thread
findings.why: In QuotaCooldowns.cs line 298, `await Task.Run(() => Apply(changes), CancellationToken.None)` is run. In `RoundEngine.cs` line 442, `AfterRoundAsync(results, cancellation.Token)` is invoked. If the server is shutting down or the round is cancelled, `Apply` uses `CancellationToken.None` and acquires `HeldFile.TakeWithin(LockPath, _lockWait)` with a 30-second timeout. Because `HeldFile.TakeWithin` performs a blocking spin (`Thread.Sleep`), if another process holds the lock or the disk is slow, server termination or round cancellation is blocked for up to 30 seconds without cancellation support.
findings.fix: Pass a cancellation token or short deadline through to `Apply` so host cancellation can abort waiting on `_lockWait` promptly.
findings.reason: Already decided in the first review (R4/fix.md): a stopped round still writes the parks and lifts it had decided, so Apply deliberately takes CancellationToken.None; the wait is bounded by the 30 s lock wait, the lock is held for milliseconds by any other writer, and the Task.Run keeps it off the async worker. Making the write cancellable would lose a decided park.

findings.title: File reading inside locked section drops previous cooldown entries if JSON deserialization throws
findings.why: In QuotaCooldowns.cs line 159, `ReadEntries(underLock: true)` is called inside `Locked()`. In `ReadEntries`, line 238 catches `JsonException` and returns `Unreadable(e)` (an empty list `[]`) even when `underLock` is true (`when (e is JsonException || (!underLock && e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException))`). If `quota-cooldowns.json` is corrupted or partially written, `Locked()` proceeds with `before = []`, folds the new round changes into an empty list, and overwrites the entire file in line 167, wiping out all previously recorded unexpired cooldown entries for other providers. DoD 4 explicitly states: 'a bad or unreadable file parks nobody and is never overwritten blindly'.
findings.fix: When `underLock: true`, if `JsonException` is caught or `read` is null/invalid in `ReadEntries`, throw an exception or return a refusal so `Locked()` refuses the write instead of overwriting the corrupted file with a fresh list containing only the new entries.
findings.reason: Same as finding 3: a JsonException under the lock is the plan's torn-file case (§8, S19), overwritten whole by the next park; an unreadable-right-now file is the one that refuses, and it does.

findings.title: Raw unredacted vendor reason is stored in cooldown file and wire note
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.cs` line 331: `new QuotaChange.Park(key, reset.UntilUtc, reset.Source, pair.Invocation.Model, $"{reset.Note}. The vendor said: {reason}")`. In `ParkedAsync`, `reason` is taken as `VendorReason.Written(limited.Reason)`. While `VendorReason.Written` applies basic sanitization, error messages from external vendor CLIs may contain user prompt text, sensitive repository paths, or raw API response fragments. This note is persisted to `quota-cooldowns.json` and broadcast over the wire in `ProviderStatus.Cooldown.Note` to VS Code and any connected MCP client.
findings.fix: Truncate and sanitize the vendor reason strictly before concatenating it into `Note`, or omit raw vendor stderr sentences from wire and shared persisted status.
findings.reason: Already covered: the reason is passed through VendorReason.Written, which is the product's one redactor (Redaction.SafeText: control characters, key blocks, credential-named values) with the safety cap, the same text the ledger and the log already write; the note is capped at 400 characters. The plan (D4/D9) specifies 'this side's sentence, then the vendor's redacted one'.

findings.title: Uncached File.ReadAllText and JSON deserialization on every standing cooldown query
findings.why: Standing() calls ReadEntries() without caching. PanelService.Cooling() is called by CanRun(), ProviderStatus mapping, and ExcludedFrom for every provider row across every stage check and 10s probe refresh. For a config with 15 provider rows across 4 stages, a single round setup triggers dozens of un-cached file reads and JSON deserializations from disk, degrading UI probe responses and roster resolution.
findings.fix: Cache the parsed QuotaCooldownFile in-memory with file timestamp/mtime invalidation or update an in-memory cache upon write, avoiding disk reads on every provider check.
findings.reason: The plan's D4 chooses 'read on every decision' on purpose (so a park by another coai-mcp process on the same data directory is seen on the next decision, and the clock ends it with no write); the file is a few hundred bytes with a ten-entry ceiling. A cache would need invalidation across processes and no measurement shows a cost; out of scope.

findings.title: Synchronous sequential probe execution across rate-limited quota keys after round completion
findings.why: AfterRoundAsync iterates through rate-limited groups with `foreach` and awaits `DecidedAsync` sequentially. If multiple providers/quotas (e.g. Gemini and Claude) are rate-limited or timing out, each AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync can wait up to 30 seconds sequentially, blocking the round from completing its summary for up to N * 30 seconds while the caller waits.
findings.fix: Run the ReadResetAsync probe tasks concurrently across distinct quota keys using Task.WhenAll before folding results into Apply().
findings.reason: Same as finding 4: sequential, one gauge call per spent key, within the plan's §8 budget; parallel probes are an enhancement outside the plan.

findings.title: Cooldown duration display switches abruptly from hours to minutes at 1 hour threshold
findings.why: Left() formats durations >= 1 hour as whole hours rounded up (`(int)Math.Ceiling(left.TotalHours) h`) and under 1 hour as minutes (`X min`). A wait of 61 minutes displays as '2 h' while 59 minutes displays as '59 min', creating a jarring jump from 2 h to 59 min in consecutive probe updates.
findings.fix: Format hours with minutes or provide smoother transitions (e.g., '1 h 1 min' or single-digit hour breakdown) to avoid sudden jumps.
findings.reason: The plan fixes the wording: D8/D9 and DoD 'the time left, rounded up' (e.g. 'in 63 h'), asserted by S31-S33. 61 minutes showing '2 h' is that rule, not a defect.

findings.title: §3 D5 and §12 let a cancelled agy probe suppress an explicit spent-quota park
findings.why: If cancellation arrives while `/quota` is being probed for a `Spent == true` outcome, §12 says that key is dropped. The completed round then writes no cooldown for it, so the next round launches the known-spent model again and can hit the long timeout this plan is meant to prevent.
findings.fix: On probe cancellation, use the explicit spent verdict's stated-reset/guess fallback and persist it; reserve dropping the key for undecided outcomes.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D5/S42 chose 'a cancelled probe parks nothing'; the code does exactly that, per key.)

findings.title: §3 D4 fail-open reads can erase a valid cooldown during a later write
findings.why: When a process cannot read the existing file—for example, it gets a transient I/O error—D4 treats that read as an empty store. If that process then acquires the lock and writes a park or lift, it can replace the unreadable-but-valid data with only its own aggregate, deleting other keys' active cooldowns. Those rows are then eligible for launch before their resets.
findings.fix: Distinguish a confirmed missing or corrupt file from a transient read failure; refuse mutations when existing state cannot be read, and report the refusal through the stated notice path.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. NOTE FOR THE CODE ROUND: QuotaCooldowns.Read() maps a transient IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException to an empty list and WrittenUnder then writes only the round's aggregate; that is a code-level question and will be judged there if raised.

findings.title: §7 and §9 do not verify the promised `--providers` compatibility path
findings.why: The plan says the one-shot `--providers` mode exposes cooldowns and that older halves safely ignore the additive field, but S29 calls `ProvidersAsync()` and S38 tests serialization only. A user invoking the actual CLI against the generated context could still receive a response with the field omitted or fail in the one-shot output path while every listed check passes.
findings.fix: Add a scenario that invokes `--providers` through its real one-shot path and asserts the cooldown JSON is present, plus a compatibility check for a consumer that ignores the unknown member.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: §3 D4, D5: Aggregating multiple keys under one file lock can deadlock or starve if post-round probes take locks or block across threads
findings.why: D4 specifies taking `quota-cooldowns.lock` via `HeldFile.TakeWithin(path, wait)` and performing a full re-read and atomic write for the aggregate of the round. While D4 states '/quota probe runs OUTSIDE the lock', D5 specifies `ReadResetAsync` is invoked during or as part of resolving key resets within `AfterRoundAsync`. If `ReadResetAsync` for agy runs concurrently or sequentially across multiple spent keys, or if multiple parallel rounds / processes attempt `AfterRoundAsync` concurrently, any process waiting up to 30s on `HeldFile` while another process holds the lock during `AtomicFile.Write` or I/O will hit `Hold.Busy` and log a `Refused` notice, leaving valid cooldowns unpersisted despite completed rounds. Concretely, two concurrent rounds completing with spent quotas on separate CLI keys will contend on the lock; the second round times out if file system operations delay the lock release, dropping cooldown persistence for that entire round.
findings.fix: Ensure `AfterRoundAsync` strictly pre-computes all probe calls and reset calculations completely in-memory before acquiring `quota-cooldowns.lock`, minimizing lock hold time to pure file read and atomic write (sub-millisecond), and document an explicit retry or queueing mechanism for `Hold.Busy` before discarding cooldown writes.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Also already covered: D4/D5 run every probe before the lock is taken, the locked section is a re-read plus one AtomicFile.Write, and a Busy lock after 30 s is an explicit Refused that becomes a server notice.)

findings.title: §3 D3, D5: Antigravity model family parsing trims only standard tiered suffixes, mishandling un-tiered or non-standard model suffixes
findings.why: D3 specifies model families are determined by 'the id minus its trailing -low / -medium / -high'. If an operator or CLI configuration passes a model identifier without these exact suffixes (e.g., bare `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-4-argon`, or future tier suffixes like `-ultra` or `-preview`), `AgyQuotaGroups.KeyOf` fails exact match in D3's table and falls through to `antigravity/?<model>`. As a concrete result, a spent quota on `gemini-3.8-flash` without a `-low`/`-medium`/`-high` suffix is classified as an unknown family, bypassing the `antigravity/gemini` shared group key and failing to gauge-park sibling Gemini models.
findings.fix: In D3 and `AgyQuotaGroups`, implement suffix stripping that handles both standard tiered suffixes (`-low`, `-medium`, `-high`) and bare family names, or explicitly normalize model names against known base family prefixes before key lookup.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Also wrong in the code: AgyQuotaGroups.WithoutEffort returns an id with no -low/-medium/-high suffix unchanged and the family table lists the bare families, so a bare gemini-3.8-flash resolves to antigravity/gemini.)

findings.title: §3 D9, §4 S31: `cooldownLine` renders empty string immediately upon expiry without triggering a webview UI refresh
findings.why: D9 specifies no active timer/ticking mechanism in the webview, relying on a 10s probe refresh in `panelProvider.ts`. If an operator is viewing the card at the exact instant `untilUtc` passes, `cooldownLine` returns `''` on the next calculation, but the card badge in `modelCardWorld.ts` still renders `cooling down` until the background probe runs and updates `reported`. For up to 10 seconds, the card displays an inconsistent UI state (badge says 'cooling down', but cooldown text line disappears).
findings.fix: Specify in D9 that `modelCardWorld.ts` evaluates both `health.cooldown` and whether `untilUtc` has passed consistently across both the line text and verdict badge, falling back to active/ready status once `nowMs >= untilUtc`.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D9 states 'no ticking' deliberately; the 10 s window is the panel's existing refresh.)

findings.title: Quota source is carried as an untyped string across the runtime boundary
findings.why: The C# doctrine says: “A business concept does not travel as a `string` or an `int`. Wrap it in a typed value with parsing and validation.” `QuotaReset.Source` is an internal business value used to decide whether to park and how to describe the cooldown, but callers compare it to string constants and can pass unsupported values.
findings.fix: Use a typed source value, such as an enum or closed record hierarchy, throughout the runtime and cooldown logic; convert it to the wire string only when serializing.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope and no defect: D4 fixes the source as the three named wire strings quota|stated|guess (QuotaSources constants, written to the file and sent to the card); a closed constant set compared in two places. A typed enum would touch the file format, the wire and every test for no behaviour change.

findings.title: Antigravity quota groups are split across independent tables that can silently disagree.
findings.why: When a future model family is added, updating `KeyByFamily` without the corresponding bucket IDs leaves its cooldown key with no gauge, so a spent quota falls back to an estimate or guess instead of using the vendor reset. The display-name table is separately maintained as well, so the same new key can appear under a raw identifier.
findings.fix: Represent each Antigravity family and quota key together in one table, including its bucket IDs and display name, and derive the lookups from that definition.
findings.reason: Minor design preference, not a defect: D3 calls for one explicit measured table, and the family table, bucket-id table and display-name table are cross-checked against the committed fixtures by S14/S43 and the key-name tests. A future family is one row plus its fixture (D3); nothing is wrong today.

findings.title: A spent bucket with no usable reset is treated as if another bucket's reset frees the quota
findings.why: If two active buckets are spent and one has a future reset while the other has no reset or only a past reset, `Judge` returns the usable bucket's reset. At that time the row is launched again even though the other quota is still spent, recreating the repeated refusal the cooldown is meant to prevent.
findings.fix: Return `SpentWithoutReset` whenever any spent bucket lacks a future reset; only return a reset instant when every spent bucket has a usable reset, using the latest instant.
findings.reason: Decided by the plan, not a code defect: D6 and S40 say 'both active at 0 with one reset_time missing or past -> Spent on the known one, the note naming the unknown'. The code does exactly that; if the unknown bucket is still spent at that instant the next refusal parks the key again (bounded, one launch).

findings.title: A probe's raw stderr is persisted and sent to the provider card
findings.why: When `/quota` exits nonzero, `ExitWhy` includes its first stderr line in `CannotCheck`; that text is then stored in the cooldown note and returned in `ProviderStatus.Cooldown`. If the command emits a credential or other sensitive diagnostic, it survives across rounds and is exposed to the card, contrary to the stated no-secret logging/notice boundary.
findings.fix: Do not persist or return raw probe stderr; use a bounded, sanitized reason such as the exit code and timeout state.
findings.reason: Already covered: the probe's stderr line is required by S15 ('exit 1: unknown command /quota'), and every note goes through VendorReason.Written -> Redaction.SafeText (key blocks, credential-named values, control characters) and the 400-character cap before it is stored or sent to the card (QuotaCooldowns.ParkedIn).

findings.title: Quota probes run sequentially before the round summary, adding up to 90 seconds with no progress indication
findings.why: If a round gets spent refusals for Antigravity Gemini, Argon, and 3p quotas and each `/quota` probe hangs, `DecideAsync` waits for each key in turn; each probe can time out after 30 seconds. `RoundEngine` awaits this method before reading the summary, so the person waits up to 90 seconds after reviews finish without seeing that cooldown checks are running.
findings.fix: Run independent key probes concurrently, while still aggregating their changes into one write, and expose a progress indication or otherwise avoid holding the round summary until probes finish.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope: D5/Budget specify one probe per spent key per round, each bounded at 30 s by the launcher; at most three agy keys exist, and only when all three are spent AND all probes hang is the delay 90 s. Concurrency or progress display is an optimisation the plan did not ask for.

findings.title: Cyclomatic complexity in Fraction exceeds the maximum limit of 4
findings.why: The rule '.agents/conventions/csharp/doctrine.md' (§6. Pure functions, small methods) states: 'Cyclomatic complexity ≤ 4 — extract, or use a switch expression.' The method 'Fraction(JsonElement bucket)' evaluates multiple conditions with 'Number(bucket) is { } fraction && fraction is >= 0 and <= 1 ? fraction : null', which yields a cyclomatic complexity of 5.
findings.fix: Simplify the condition or use a switch expression, e.g.: `private static double? Fraction(JsonElement bucket) => Number(bucket) is >= 0 and <= 1 and var fraction ? fraction : null;` or extract the range check.
findings.reason: Wrong: by Roslyn's count (?: + && + 'and' pattern) Fraction is 4, which the bound allows; CA1502 is not enabled for this file (.editorconfig switches it on for the security lane's files only).

findings.title: Cyclomatic complexity in TryGroups exceeds the maximum limit of 4
findings.why: The rule '.agents/conventions/csharp/doctrine.md' (§6. Pure functions, small methods) states: 'Cyclomatic complexity ≤ 4 — extract, or use a switch expression.' The method 'TryGroups' chains four boolean AND conditions (`Child(root, ...) && Child(command, ...) && Child(data, ...) && groups.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array`), resulting in a cyclomatic complexity of 5.
findings.fix: Split the property lookups across separate statements or use pattern matching to keep cyclomatic complexity ≤ 4.
findings.reason: Wrong: TryGroups is 1 + three && = 4, which the bound allows (the 4th operand is the right side of the third &&); CA1502 is not enabled for this file.

findings.title: Cyclomatic complexity in Number exceeds the maximum limit of 4
findings.why: The rule '.agents/conventions/csharp/doctrine.md' (§6. Pure functions, small methods) states: 'Cyclomatic complexity ≤ 4 — extract, or use a switch expression.' The method 'Number' checks `Child(...) && value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Number && value.TryGetDouble(...)`, which has multiple branches and boundary conditions.
findings.fix: Decompose into smaller helper methods or use a direct switch expression to ensure cyclomatic complexity is ≤ 4.
findings.reason: Wrong: Number is 1 + two && + one ?: = 4, which the bound allows, and the reviewer itself marks it non-gating.

findings.title: Probe reset lookup bypasses invocation adapter, forcing agy probes through default launcher
findings.why: ResetOfAsync calls first.Invocation.Adapter!.ReadResetAsync(..., Launcher, ...). Invocation carries both an Adapter (IReviewerRuntime) and an Invoker/Launcher context. Passing the store-level Launcher rather than the invocation's runtime launcher/context breaks per-invocation execution settings (e.g. custom environment, working directory, or mock wrappers configured during invocation setup) and violates encapsulation by making QuotaCooldowns own the launcher for all reviewer runtimes.
findings.fix: Pass invocation.Launcher if present, or let the runtime resolve its launcher from the invocation instance.
findings.reason: Wrong: the probe runs the refused invocation's OWN request (executable, environment, working directory via invocation.Request with {...}); only the process launcher is the store's, as D5 specifies (ReadResetAsync takes an IProcessLauncher) so tests can fake it. ReviewerInvocation has no launcher of its own.

findings.title: Apply uses a synchronous lock wait with HeldFile.TakeWithin inside an async pipeline
findings.why: AfterRoundAsync is called on an async round completion path and offloads Apply via Task.Run (() => Apply(changes)). However, HeldFile.TakeWithin uses synchronous thread-blocking file-lock polling for up to 30 seconds. In containerized or constrained thread-pool environments, holding worker threads in synchronous file-lock polling blocks the thread pool and couples round completion to disk lock contention.
findings.fix: Use an asynchronous file lock acquisition pattern or cancellation-aware async polling to acquire the lock.
findings.reason: Already covered and plan-mandated: D4 requires HeldFile.TakeWithin (the product's one cross-process primitive); the previous review already moved the wait off the async thread with Task.Run (TheWriteWaitsForItsLockOffTheCallersThread). An async lock primitive is a new primitive, outside this plan.

findings.title: AskingOf filter drops Spent == false but doesn't check RateLimit.Hopeless when Spent is null
findings.why: When Spent is null (undecided), AskingOf treats every RateLimited row as needing a reset probe. For runtimes where Hopeless is false and Spent is null, this triggers unnecessary probe requests and log noise instead of recognizing transient errors early.
findings.fix: Filter asking rows to those where Spent == true or RateLimit.Hopeless(row.Outcome.Reason).
findings.reason: Wrong/already covered: the default ReadResetAsync answers NoPark('a transient refusal; nothing parked') for Spent==null with a non-hopeless reason without any process launch; only agy's override probes, and D5 requires the gauge to decide agy's undecided case.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse calculates the JSON body offset incorrectly when Token appears after leading whitespace
findings.why: In `Parse`, `line` is computed using `stderr.AsSpan(from, lineEnd - from).TrimStart()`, so `line.Length` excludes leading spaces on that line. However, `stderr[(lineEnd - line.Length + Token.Length)..]` assumes `lineEnd - line.Length` points to the start of `line` in `stderr`. If `stderr` contains leading whitespace on the AGY_ERROR line (e.g. '   AGY_ERROR {...}'), `lineEnd - line.Length` lands after the start of `AGY_ERROR`, causing the slice to start in the middle of or past `Token` and cut into the JSON body. `FromBody` receives a mangled string, `FromJson` fails with `JsonException` and returns null, silently dropping the error verdict and failing to park a spent quota.
findings.fix: Locate the token cleanly using `from + lineSpan.IndexOf(Token, StringComparison.Ordinal) + Token.Length` or slice `line` directly after `Token.Length` and pass that remainder to `FromBody`.
findings.reason: Wrong, checked by arithmetic: line = span(from..lineEnd).TrimStart() so line.Length = (lineEnd-from) - leadingSpaces, and lineEnd - line.Length = from + leadingSpaces = the index of 'A' of AGY_ERROR; adding Token.Length lands right after the token. Indented tokens are read correctly. I add a pinning test for the indented line (green at once) so the claim is no longer unpinned.

findings.title: Task.Run unobserved exception can crash the process or leave quota changes uncommitted
findings.why: `AfterRoundAsync` invokes `await Task.Run(() => Apply(changes), CancellationToken.None);`. In Native-AOT and .NET runtime environments, if `Apply` throws an unhandled exception (for instance, an unexpected file system exception from `HeldFile.TakeWithin` or `Path.Combine` that is not caught inside `TryCreateDataDir` / `Persisted`), awaiting `Task.Run` rethrows. More critically, the method remarks and plan state that `AfterRoundAsync` must NEVER throw past the engine or fail the round. If `Apply` throws, `AfterRoundAsync` crashes the round or leaves completed results unhandled in callers expecting completion.
findings.fix: Wrap the `Apply(changes)` invocation in `Task.Run` in a `try/catch (Exception e)` block that logs the failure and calls `Refuse` or records the warning without throwing.
findings.reason: Real gap against the stated contract (AfterRoundAsync never throws past the engine; RoundEngine awaits it unguarded): Directory.CreateDirectory throws ArgumentException/NotSupportedException for a data dir path the catch does not list, and that escapes Apply through Task.Run. Fix test-first.

findings.title: Usable ignores buckets when reset_time equals nowUtc, treating zero-duration reset as unusable
findings.why: In `Usable`, `bucket.ResetTime is { } reset && reset > nowUtc` rejects buckets where `reset == nowUtc`. If a vendor quota report indicates a reset time that has just elapsed or is exactly aligned with `nowUtc`, all spent buckets are marked unusable, leading `Judge` to return `SpentWithoutReset` instead of recognizing that the quota reset has arrived or fallen back predictably.
findings.fix: Ensure that `Usable` handles the boundary condition or checks `reset >= nowUtc`, or cleanly distinguishes an expired reset from an unknown reset time.
findings.reason: Decided by the plan: D6 says a bucket 'whose reset_time is not after nowUtc' is no reset, never a park on the past; QuotaCooldowns.Standing treats untilUtc == now as already back, so the strict comparison is consistent. S40 pins the past case.

findings.title: WarnOnce only logs the first error ever encountered across all read cycles
findings.why: `WarnOnce` uses `Interlocked.Exchange(ref _warned, 1) == 0` without resetting `_warned`. If a transient read or JSON parse error occurs at startup and logs once, any subsequent corruption or permissions error occurring days later will be completely silent and fail open without any notice or log entry.
findings.fix: Reset `_warned` periodically upon a successful read, or key the warning by the specific file path or error cause.
findings.reason: Decided by the plan: D4 says 'logging once per process' for an unreadable file (S19 pins exactly one warning after three reads). Non-gating.

findings.title: Quadratic string allocations and substring copying when parsing AGY_ERROR tokens
findings.why: In `AgyError.Parse`, when a line begins with `AGY_ERROR`, it allocates a substring across the remainder of the entire stderr buffer (`stderr[(lineEnd - line.Length + Token.Length)..]`), and then `FromBody` slices it again before `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(json)` copies and converts the entire remainder of `stderr` into a byte array for `Utf8JsonReader`. If `stderr` is large (e.g. 50 KB of debug/stream output with multiple error lines or verbose output), every matched token allocates new multi-kilobyte strings and byte arrays on the hot error parsing path.
findings.fix: Pass a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` or parse directly from `ReadOnlySpan<char>` without allocating the rest of `stderr`, or find the matching closing brace index for the JSON object before converting to bytes.
findings.reason: Not a defect: the parse runs once per refused launch on a bounded stderr that the executor has already redacted and capped; no hot path. Speculative micro-optimisation outside the plan.

findings.title: Sequential quota probe executions stall post-round completion when multiple quota keys are exhausted
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.AfterRoundAsync`, `DecideAsync` is called sequentially in a `foreach (var group in KeyedBy(results))` loop. Each `DecideAsync` invokes `AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync`, which spawns external CLI processes with a 30-second timeout. If multiple models fail on quota limits across multiple keys (e.g. Gemini and Argon or ThirdParty), the round is delayed by the sum of their probe execution times (up to N * 30 seconds) before returning results to the caller.
findings.fix: Execute the probe decisions concurrently across distinct quota keys using `Task.WhenAll` over `KeyedBy(results)`.
findings.reason: Duplicate of the sequential-probe finding: outside the plan's scope (one probe per spent key, each bounded at 30 s); not a defect.

findings.title: Partially expired multi-bucket verdict masks the known bucket reset window
findings.why: When multiple buckets are spent and only a subset have valid future reset times (`usable.Count < spent.Count`), `Judge` formats the note as `$"{usable[0].Window}; {unusable.Window} reset unknown"`. If multiple usable buckets exist, only `usable[0]` is mentioned while others are silently omitted from the explanation, and if `unusable` is chosen via `First()`, other unusable buckets are not reported, misleading the operator about which quotas are cooling.
findings.fix: Join all usable windows (e.g. `string.Join(" and ", usable.Select(b => b.Window))`) in the note so the operator sees every bucket contributing to the cooldown.
findings.reason: Minor wording of a note whose exact shape the plan fixes (S40: 'weekly; 5h reset unknown'); every bucket's window is still named in the all-usable case. Non-gating.

findings.title: Section 3 D3: Missing vendor routing enforcement for claude models via agy in QuotaKeyOf creates quota leaks violating local.common.vendor-routing
findings.why: D3 maps claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 under Antigravity to 'antigravity/3p', noting 'local.common.vendor-routing still forbids a Claude model on agy; the 3p row is for GPT-OSS and for an agy row somebody configures against that rule'. However, neither D3 nor PanelService.CanRun enforces or checks vendor-routing to block such configured rows from executing via agy. If a user configures a Claude reviewer on agy, the system executes it against agy's metered subscription instead of blocking it, depleting quota as recorded in vendor-routing.md.
findings.fix: In AntigravityRuntime or PanelService.CanRun, explicitly reject or refuse execution if a Claude model is routed to the agy adapter, enforcing the vendor-routing rule rather than enabling and tracking it under antigravity/3p.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D3 names vendor-routing on purpose and routing enforcement is not this plan's scope; no defect in the code seen.)

findings.title: Section 3 D12: Unilateral rejection of required epic breakdown violates project conventions for large plans
findings.why: Section 3 D12 and Section 11 explicitly state that the author declined the operator's standing commands and project conventions to split the plan into epics (as mandated by planning-docs.md § 'A plan split into epics and stories'). Omitting the epic breakdown and cornerstone ledgers prevents plan lifecycle checks (plan-lifecycle.mjs) from tracking story cornerstones and parent/child plan promotions.
findings.fix: Structure the plan into ## Epics with corresponding todo/PLAN_*_E<n>.md documents and cornerstone ledger lines in accordance with .agents/conventions/common/planning-docs.md.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The one-file, no-epics shape is the owner's recorded decision, D12/§11.)

findings.title: Section 3 D6: Missing timeout cancellation handling in AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync can hang rounds or leak child processes
findings.why: D6 specifies cloning the request with 'Timeout = 30 s' and running through IProcessLauncher, while D5 specifies that AfterRoundAsync passes the round's CancellationToken. If the round's token is cancelled while the process is running, or if IProcessLauncher's timeout fires, external-process rules (common.security) mandate calling Process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true). If the probe wrapper in AgyQuotaProbe does not tie the round's cancellation token directly to tree killing, an orphaned CLI process will hold locks and credentials.
findings.fix: Explicitly specify in D6 that AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync binds the passed CancellationToken and 30s timeout to process tree termination via Process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true) before returning CannotCheck.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The probe goes through IProcessLauncher, whose timeout kills the tree; cancellation is covered by S42 and the review fix 2f2e1381.)

findings.title: D4/D5 can turn a failed cooldown read into an unlocked write that erases active parks
findings.why: The plan says a torn or unreadable file means “no cooldown” and then says the next park overwrites it whole. For example, if the file contains an active Gemini park plus malformed JSON, `Standing` fails open; a later Claude park cannot recover the Gemini entry and writes only Claude. Multiple servers can then launch the still-spent Gemini row, despite the cross-process lock serializing the write.
findings.fix: Distinguish a known-empty file from an unreadable file. Refuse mutations while the existing state cannot be read, notify the person, and preserve the damaged file for recovery instead of replacing it as an empty aggregate.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (An unreadable file read as no cooldown and overwritten whole by the next park is the plan's decided behaviour, S19/§8; the code does exactly that.)

findings.title: D5 lifts a quota-wide cooldown when any sibling row succeeds, even if another sibling just proved the quota is spent
findings.why: For one key, the plan says a qualifying spent outcome wins over `Ok` when parking, but does not make that precedence apply to an already-standing entry during a round with no new qualifying refusal. If Gemini row A is parked and row B is enabled or becomes runnable through a concurrent state change, B can succeed while A produces only a timeout; the aggregate's “a key with an `Ok` and no qualifying refusal is lifted” removes the key-wide park and the next round launches A again.
findings.fix: Define one per-key precedence for existing and new state: a fresh qualifying spent outcome must park, otherwise lift only when the successful launch is valid evidence for the same quota and no sibling outcome contradicts it; specify and test the mixed `Ok` plus timeout case against an already-standing entry.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D5 states the rule: a key with an Ok and no qualifying refusal is lifted, S25.)

findings.title: D9 hides a cooldown from a second row sharing the quota key
findings.why: `ProbeAsync` attaches the cooldown using the row's quota key, but the plan's scenario only checks one cooling row and one row in another group. If two configured rows share `antigravity/gemini`, a provider probe that iterates or de-duplicates by row can report the cooldown on only one row; the other card can still say `coai-mcp will run it` even though `CanRun` excludes it. The plan promises the card tells the person why a row is out, but does not verify the same-key multi-row case.
findings.fix: Add a provider response and running-card scenario with two rows sharing one quota key, asserting both carry the same cooldown and both show the cooling badge.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (No defect seen in the code: PanelService.ProbeAsync attaches Standing(provider) to every row by its own quota key, so two rows sharing a key both carry it.)

findings.title: D5 cancels the only quota probe without defining a retry path for a spent refusal
findings.why: When the round token is cancelled while `/quota` is running, S42 requires the probe to park nothing. If the host stops the round after the refusal and before another round runs, no persistent state records the known spent result; when work resumes, the same model is launched again and can consume its full timeout or fail again.
findings.fix: On cancellation, persist the explicitly spent refusal using its stated reset or marked guess without waiting for the probe, or define and verify a guaranteed retry before any affected row can be launched again.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (S42 decides that a cancelled probe parks nothing; the next round's refusal parks it.)

findings.title: An undecided refusal whose gauge confirms a spent bucket without reset_time is never parked
findings.why: When an agy launch fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED without the 'Individual quota reached' sentence, its verdict is undecided (spent == null). At round end, ReadResetAsync probes /quota. If /quota confirms the bucket is spent (remaining_fraction is 0) but carries no future reset_time, ResetFor returns QuotaGauge.SpentWithoutReset. Line 110 routes this to Undecided(spent, ...). In Undecided, the condition 'spent == true' is false for null, returning QuotaReset.NotParked. Consequently, despite the vendor's gauge confirming the quota bucket is depleted to 0, the model is never parked and will be launched repeatedly in subsequent rounds into the same spent limit.
findings.fix: In AntigravityRuntime.ReadResetAsync, handle QuotaGauge.SpentWithoutReset by calling QuotaReset.FromText(reason, consecutive, nowUtc, $... reads {name} as spent but names no reset time.) so it falls back to coai's guess interval regardless of whether spent was initially true, or pass spent ?? true to Undecided.
findings.reason: This is the plan's decided behaviour: D10 says an undecided agy refusal with a spent bucket that has no reset_time is 'cannot check' and parks nothing, and D5 says 'the issue's undetermined is never a parked row'. The previous review (R3) settled exactly this: a refusal the vendor called spent still parks on the text, an undecided one parks nothing; test ASpentBucketWithoutAResetTime_ParksOnlyARefusalTheVendorCalledSpent pins it.

findings.title: AgyQuotaReport.Candidates splits multi-line JSON into invalid individual lines when stdout contains preamble text
findings.why: If agy outputs any diagnostic message, banner, or update check before or after the multi-line JSON response, Parse first attempts stdout.Trim(), which fails with JsonException due to the non-JSON preamble. Candidates then falls back to iterating stdout.Split('\n') lines starting with '{'. Because the JSON output is pretty-printed across multiple lines, individual lines like '{' fail to parse as independent JSON documents. This causes Parse to return AgyQuotaReport.None and report 'no report in the answer', turning a successful /quota execution into QuotaGauge.CannotCheck.
findings.fix: When stdout.Trim() fails to parse as JSON, slice the candidate substring from stdout.IndexOf('{') to stdout.LastIndexOf('}') + 1 rather than splitting by newline.
findings.reason: Not observed and outside D6: the real /quota capture (agy 1.4.9, exit 0, stderr empty) is one JSON document on stdout; banners and diagnostics go to stderr, and the plan reads 'the whole document, or the last line that is one'. Speculative hardening against output nobody has seen; if a preamble appears the probe is CannotCheck, which parks nothing it did not know (fails safe).

findings.title: DecidedOrNullAsync only catches OperationCanceledException, causing any unexpected probe or parser failure to abort all round cooldown updates
findings.why: DecidedOrNullAsync wraps DecidedAsync in a try/catch that catches only OperationCanceledException. If launcher invocation or parsing for one key throws an unexpected runtime exception (e.g., unexpected process startup failure, OS permission error, or malformed data in ResetOfAsync), the exception escapes ChangesAsync to the catch block in AfterRoundAsync. This aborts processing of the entire results list, preventing all other unaffected keys from being parked or lifted for that round.
findings.fix: In DecidedOrNullAsync, catch general Exception, log that the key's cooldown decision failed, and return null so sibling keys' cooldown decisions are still collected and applied.
findings.reason: Real: any non-cancellation throw from one key's decision escaped to AfterRoundAsync and voided every other key's park/lift. Fixed with a catch in DecidedOrNullAsync that logs the key; test AProbeThatThrows_DoesNotVoidTheOtherKeysOfTheRound was red (codex park lost).

findings.title: The cross-module cooldown flow is documented without updating the architecture entry point.
findings.why: The change adds a flow across the MCP server and extension, but the diff updates their module docs without updating `research/architecture.md`. The project rule says: “If cross-module or cross-repository interaction changed — update `research/architecture.md` too.”
findings.fix: Update `research/architecture.md` to describe the cooldown flow between the server and extension, and re-render any affected diagrams.
findings.reason: The knowledge-base rule asks for research/architecture.md when cross-module interaction changed, and this change adds a server-to-extension wire member. Added a short section beside the 'older half' seam section.

findings.title: A valid JSON cooldown file with a null entry bypasses the fail-open read handling
findings.why: If the file contains `{"v":1,"entries":[null]}`, deserialization can produce a non-null `Entries` list containing a null element. `Read()` accepts it, then `Standing()` dereferences `entry.Key`; the exception escapes and can break provider or roster requests instead of treating the unreadable file as no cooldown, as the documented fail-open behavior requires.
findings.fix: Validate deserialized entries before returning the file: reject null entries and entries with invalid required fields, log once, and return `Empty`.
findings.reason: Real: {"v":1,"entries":[null]} parsed and then threw NullReferenceException out of Standing, breaking the fail-open contract of D4. Read() now treats a null element as an unreadable file (one warning, no cooldown); test AValidFileWithANullEntry_ParksNobody_AndTheNextParkWritesItWhole was red with the NullReferenceException.

findings.title: The post-round quota probe can add a 30-second wait for each spent key in sequence.
findings.why: With, for example, spent Codex, Claude, Kimi, and Antigravity rows in one round, `ChangesAsync` awaits each key's reset probe sequentially. If every agy probe times out, later keys are not settled until earlier 30-second timeouts finish, so the completed round summary is delayed by up to 90 seconds even though probes use independent accounts and the plan only requires one probe per key.
findings.fix: Run independent per-key decisions concurrently, while retaining one aggregated locked write after they finish; ensure cancellation of one probe only drops that key's decision.
findings.reason: Outside the plan: D5/section 8 specify one probe per spent key, each bounded at 30 s by the launcher, and say nothing of concurrency. Only agy keys launch a probe at all (codex, claude and kimi read their reset from text), so the worst case is up to three agy probes all timing out; running them concurrently adds ordering and cancellation complexity for a rare case the plan did not ask for.

findings.title: Probe clones invocation request with its review working folder instead of standard Home()
findings.why: AgyQuotaProbe creates request via 'invocation.Request with { Arguments = Arguments ... }'. For code rounds, invocation.Request.WorkingFolder is pinned to a temporary git worktree outside the repo which is pruned/deleted in 'finally' after the round. Slash commands like '/quota' run in an arbitrary review worktree instead of AntigravityReadOnly.Home(). If the worktree is concurrently cleaned up, locked, or if agy expects a persistent/clean home environment, probe execution can fail, or worse, agy execution inside the ephemeral worktree violates the documented architecture boundary where reviewer background commands should execute against AntigravityReadOnly.Home().
findings.fix: Explicitly set WorkingFolder to AntigravityReadOnly.Home() on the cloned request in AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync, matching the class documentation remarks.
findings.reason: Wrong: AntigravityRuntime builds every agy request with AntigravityReadOnly.Home() as its working folder (AntigravityRuntime.cs:64) — the review worktree is passed as an --add-dir style workspace argument, not as the working folder — so the cloned probe request already runs in Home(), exactly as D6 requires and S15 asserts.

findings.title: SequenceEqual on reference types bypasses no-op write guard for QuotaCooldownEntry lists
findings.why: In WrittenUnder, 'entries.SequenceEqual(onDisk)' is used to avoid writing to disk when a change is a no-op (such as lifting a key that is not in onDisk). However, 'standing' filters out expired items, creating a new list instance, and if any entry is re-entered or refreshed, or when comparing against deserialized records without custom list equality or when elements are reordered, SequenceEqual compares entries. If elements exist, but a key is lifted that was not present, entries is reconstructed from standing (which are reference elements of onDisk). But if there were expired entries on disk that got dropped in 'standing', onDisk.Count != standing.Count, so SequenceEqual is false and it writes (which is fine). But if entries has the exact same content, SequenceEqual works because QuotaCooldownEntry is a record. However, if onDisk has multiple entries and Applied removes/appends to the end via collection expressions, the order changes (the modified/unaffected entries are ordered differently from onDisk), causing SequenceEqual to return false and force an unnecessary atomic write on every round evaluation.
findings.fix: Preserve list ordering when applying changes or compare by key set / entry equality independently of collection order before determining if the file changed.
findings.reason: Wrong: the guard is for a lift of a key that does not stand; there Applied returns the same standing entries in the same order, so SequenceEqual is true and nothing is written. A park or a lift of a standing key changes the list and is rightly written. A reorder of untouched entries cannot cause a write that was not otherwise due.

findings.title: Ended grouping uses raw model instead of adapter-normalized model name
findings.why: In QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs, ByKey groups by 'ended.Invocation.Adapter!.QuotaKeyOf(ended.Invocation.Model)'. In AntigravityRuntime, QuotaKeyOf checks 'model.Length > 0 ? model : DefaultModel'. However, if Invocation.Model is null or whitespace on other runtimes, or if Invocation.Model differs in casing from settings, QuotaKeyOf returns different keys or throws if an adapter assumes non-null string, creating inconsistent quota key partitions across callers.
findings.fix: Ensure invocation model is passed as (ended.Invocation.Model ?? string.Empty).Trim() or normalize model in QuotaKeyOf across all adapters.
findings.reason: Speculative and outside the plan: QuotaKeyOf is a fixed table (D3) over the configured model id; no caller passes a differently cased or null model, and an unknown id gets its own key by design.

findings.title: Standing performs unbuffered disk I/O and JSON deserialization on hot paths with zero caching
findings.why: Every single invocation of Standing reads the file from disk (File.ReadAllText) and deserializes JSON afresh via Read(). Standing is evaluated repeatedly during model roster construction and readiness checks (CanRun, panel probe for all configured models, etc.). Across multiple reviewer checks or frequent panel refresh polling (every 10 seconds), this causes redundant synchronous disk reads and allocations instead of checking an in-memory cached copy invalidated by writes or file mtime.
findings.fix: Cache the deserialized entries and timestamp/mtime in memory within QuotaCooldowns, re-reading from disk only when File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc changes or after a local mutation.
findings.reason: The plan decided this: D4 says 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever, §8)', so that another process's park is seen on the next decision. The panel's 10 s refresh over a file of at most ten small entries is not a hot path.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse allocates split arrays and parses JSON documents for every line across the entire stderr buffer
findings.why: Parse executes stderr.Split('\n') and processes lines without bounding size. When a reviewer process fails with noisy or voluminous stderr (e.g. hundreds of kilobytes of stack trace, logs, or payload dumps), this allocates many string instances and repeatedly invokes JsonDocument.Parse on each candidate line, running on the synchronous execution path of the runner.
findings.fix: Inspect candidate lines using ReadOnlySpan<char> or a line enumerator, verify the AGY_ERROR prefix before any substring allocation, and limit parsing to matching prefix slices.
findings.reason: Outside this plan's scope and unmeasured: AgyError.Parse runs only on the failure path of an agy launch, over stderr the executor has already capped and redacted, and it checks the AGY_ERROR prefix before parsing a line; no measured cost is given.

findings.title: AgyQuotaProbe imposes an unnotified 30-second tree-killing blocking delay when the agy CLI hangs or rate-limits /quota
findings.why: When agy CLI hangs on /quota or Antigravity's API stalls, ReadAsync blocks the post-round completion pipeline for up to 30 seconds before killing the process tree, during which no progress update or status is reported to the user waiting for round completion.
findings.fix: Lower the probe timeout to a tighter bound (e.g., 5-10s) matching CLI interactive responsiveness, or emit a progress notice before awaiting the probe.
findings.reason: The plan decided this: D6 and §8 fix the probe at 30 s, bounded by the launcher's own tree-killing timeout; a tighter bound is a plan change, and the owner's own command carries --print-timeout 20s.

findings.title: The default quota key lets a new quota-aware runtime silently skip cooldown persistence
findings.why: When someone adds a reviewer runtime that classifies a spent allowance through `RateLimited` but forgets to override `QuotaKeyOf`, the default empty key causes `QuotaCooldowns.ByKey` to discard its outcomes. The runtime continues launching against the spent allowance every round without any indication that its cooldown was never recorded.
findings.fix: Make `QuotaKeyOf` an explicit implementation requirement, or add a capability contract that requires quota-aware runtimes to declare their keying behavior.
findings.reason: The plan decided this: D3 makes the empty key the default on purpose ('empty means this runtime has no quota coai parks') and lists which runtimes override it; making it abstract would force a key on runtimes that have none (local, api, remote).

findings.title: A corrupt or incompatible cooldown file is silently replaced by an empty file on the next mutation
findings.why: If the file parses but is missing required entry fields, contains an invalid timestamp, or has an unsupported schema version, `Read()` returns an empty state.
