A subsequent park or lift re-reads the same empty state under the lock and writes a fresh file, discarding every previously parked quota. For example, after a future version writes `v:2` or one entry's timestamp is malformed, a round can overwrite the file with only its current changes and allow other still-spent quotas to run again.
findings.fix: Validate the version and every entry before treating the file as writable; on invalid input, preserve/refuse mutation and surface a notice rather than replacing it with an empty file.
findings.reason: The plan decided this: a file that cannot be read is no cooldown and the next park overwrites it whole (D4, S19, §8) — the same finding was rejected in the plan round on the same grounds. A refusing mode would leave a damaged file blocking every later park.

findings.title: The probe includes the first stderr line in an error value without applying the launcher's redaction
findings.why: When `agy /quota` exits nonzero, `FirstLine(result.StdErr)` is passed to `VendorReason.Written`, but the probe request inherits the original invocation's environment, including `ANTIGRAVITY_API_KEY`. If the CLI echoes that key in its first error line, the cooldown note is persisted and later exposed in the providers answer and card tooltip. The code comment calls this line redacted, but this probe path does not demonstrate that it is.
findings.fix: Run the first stderr line through the same secret-redaction path used for reviewer launch errors before placing it in `Why` or persisting it.
findings.reason: Already covered: the line goes through VendorReason.Written, the product's one redactor (Redaction.SafeText: control characters, key blocks, credential-named values, recognisable shapes), capped; the note is that redacted text. Echoing the API key from a failed /quota is hypothetical and no different from any other launch's stderr.

findings.title: Sequential quota probes can delay the round summary without showing progress.
findings.why: After a round with spent quotas in all three Antigravity groups, `ChangesAsync` waits for each probe in turn, and each may run for 30 seconds. The summary can therefore be delayed by up to 90 seconds after reviews finish, with no progress indication during that wait.
findings.fix: Expose probe progress while settling the round, or run independent key probes concurrently while retaining one probe per key and the existing per-key failure handling.
findings.reason: Already decided in round 1 of this stage: one probe per spent key, each bounded at 30 s (D5, §8), and only agy keys probe at all; concurrency or a progress notice is not in the plan.

findings.title: Each provider row reparses the entire cooldown file when checking its status.
findings.why: `Standing` calls `QuotaCooldowns.Standing`, which reads and deserializes the file on every call. For 1,000 provider rows and 1,000 parked keys, roster and providers-answer construction can trigger thousands of disk reads and repeatedly scan up to 1,000 entries, making this work grow roughly with rows multiplied by parked keys.
findings.fix: Read the cooldown file once per roster or providers-answer operation and reuse that snapshot for its rows, while retaining fresh reads at the next operation so other processes' writes are observed.
findings.reason: The plan decided this: D4 reads the file on every decision with no cache, and the file is under 16 KiB with at most about ten entries (§8); a thousand rows and a thousand parked keys is not a state this product can reach.

findings.title: §8's 16 KiB cooldown-file ceiling is not enforced for unknown Antigravity model keys
findings.why: D3 assigns each unknown configured model its own `antigravity/?<model>` key, while §8 says the file is capped at 16 KiB and retained forever except for expiry or success. If an operator configures many unknown models and each is refused before its stated reset expires, each refusal can add another entry; the stated under-ten estimate is not a bound. The file can exceed its declared ceiling, contradicting the storage budget and the read-path assumption that it stays under 16 KiB.
findings.fix: Enforce a hard bound on entries or serialized size, with a defined refusal policy that does not evict an active cooldown; alternatively, bound the accepted unknown-model keys at configuration time and revise the projected-size claim.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Code check: entries are pruned on every write and S20 holds the file under 16 KiB; the keys are a closed set plus one per configured unknown agy model, so no defect is visible in the code.)

findings.title: §6's suite does not verify that an Antigravity probe failure leaves an explicitly spent refusal parked
findings.why: D5 requires an explicitly spent (`Spent == true`) refusal to fall back to the stated reset or guess when `/quota` cannot be checked. S23 checks a failed probe with a stated-reset reason, but no named scenario covers a failed probe when the reason has no parseable reset and must use the guess. A regression that returns `Parks == false` for this failure would leave the spent model eligible next round and recreate the repeated launch the plan is meant to stop.
findings.fix: Add a scenario with `Spent == true`, a reset-free reason, and a failed or timed-out probe; assert that it parks under the key with `source == "guess"` and records why the probe could not be checked.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: §4 and §7 leave a timed-out `/quota` process's cleanup unverified
findings.why: S15 checks that a timed-out probe returns `CannotCheck`, and §8 asserts the shared launcher's timeout kills the process tree, but the scenarios never assert that a timed-out `/quota` child and its descendants are gone before the launcher returns. If the timeout only stops waiting, repeated rounds can leave orphaned `agy` processes holding resources while the cooldown path reports an ordinary failed check.
findings.fix: Add a process-launcher integration scenario for the probe timeout that starts a child with a descendant, triggers the timeout, and verifies the entire tree is terminated before the launch returns.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: D4 and D5: Lock acquisition failure in AfterRoundAsync completely bypasses quota cooldown without retry or fallback
findings.why: In D4, HeldFile.TakeWithin returns Hold.Busy after the 30s timeout or Hold.Unusable, producing CooldownWrite.Refused(why), which AfterRoundAsync logs and records as a notice without retrying or persisting. If multiple rounds finish concurrently or another process holds quota-cooldowns.lock for >30s, the entire round's cooldown mutations (both parks and lifts) are permanently dropped. On the next round, the spent model is immediately re-included in the roster instead of being parked, leading directly to the 30-minute timeout/failure loop that issue #878 was created to stop.
findings.fix: In AfterRoundAsync, when a lock write is refused due to timeout/contention, schedule a background retry or stage the pending aggregate mutations into an in-memory/fallback queue so the next round or subsequent check acquires the lock and persists the park before building the next roster.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D4 deliberately makes a refused write an explicit refusal that never touches the round's results.)

findings.title: D4 and D6: Sibling concurrent rounds independently spawn redundant /quota probes outside the lock
findings.why: D4 states that the /quota probe runs outside the lock, before it. When two or more coai-mcp rounds run concurrently across different processes or worktrees sharing the data directory, both see spent outcomes simultaneously and both spawn independent agy -p /quota processes at the exact moment the account is in RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Multiple concurrent CLI calls against an already exhausted or rate-limited provider CLI can trigger further CLI rate-limiting, contention, or timeouts.
findings.fix: Coordinate probe execution across processes using a lightweight lock/timestamp check or cache the probe result briefly in quota-cooldowns.json so that a probe run within the last 60 seconds satisfies sibling processes without launching redundant child CLI processes.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (D4/§8 already state the probe runs outside the lock, one child per spent key per round, with no cache.)

findings.title: D8 and D9: Incompatible 24-hour hourCycle and locale in cooldownLine formatting
findings.why: D8 specifies formatting with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { day, month, year, hour, minute, hourCycle: 'h23' }) expecting 'dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm'. However, the 'en-GB' locale standardly formats dates with slashes ('dd/MM/yyyy, HH:mm') rather than periods (dots). S31 and D9 expect dot-separated dates ('14.10.2026 09:19'). The standard en-GB format will fail strict equality assertions against dot-delimited expectations or require custom string replacement that the plan does not define.
findings.fix: Explicitly specify in D8/D9 that cooldownLine either formats part-by-part using formatToParts to assemble the 'dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm' string or uses a custom formatter to ensure dot separators across Node and browser environments.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Code check: cooldownWords.ts builds the string from Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB').formatToParts, so the dot-separated dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm is assembled part by part, not taken from the locale string; no defect.)

findings.title: The quota tests mutate parsed JSON objects to construct fixtures
findings.why: The project rule says, “ALWAYS create new objects, NEVER mutate existing ones.” `Edited` parses a JSON object and then changes its bucket properties in place; other new quota tests use the same approach. This makes fixture construction depend on mutation instead of producing a new value.
findings.fix: Build each edited fixture as a new JSON value, or use immutable fixture data and serialize a new object with the desired bucket values.
findings.reason: Wrong: the test helper Edited parses a FRESH JsonNode from the committed fixture text on every call and changes that private copy before serializing it; no shared or existing object is mutated, and nothing outside the helper can see the node. The immutability rule is about shared state, not a locally built fixture.

findings.title: A cancelled round can still mutate durable quota state
findings.why: The post-round hook receives `cancellation.Token`, and `AfterRoundAsync` uses it only for quota probes before committing. If there are no agy probes—for example, a Claude or Codex refusal with a stated reset—the token is never checked; the method proceeds to `Mutate` and parks the quota after the round was cancelled. That violates the stated invariant that a cancelled round parks nothing and couples cancellation behaviour to which runtime happened to refuse.
findings.fix: Check the cancellation token before any quota-state mutation, and return without applying the aggregate when the round is cancelled.
findings.reason: Outside the plan: D5/S42 specify that a cancelled or stopped PROBE parks nothing (already fixed and tested in 74312833). A refusal that already ended in the round's results (RateLimited, with the vendor's own words) is evidence the quota is spent whether or not the round was cancelled afterwards; a cancelled reviewer's outcome is Cancelled, not RateLimited, so no cancelled launch is ever parked. The scope text's 'a cancelled round parks nothing' was a loose paraphrase; the plan's sentence is about the probe.

findings.title: Cooldown writes do not enforce the promised 16 KiB file limit.
findings.why: Each unknown Antigravity model gets its own quota key, and `ParkOp` appends an entry for each distinct key while only capping the note length. If enough models are refused before their cooldowns expire, serialization can exceed 16 KiB despite every write succeeding, violating the file-size bound and allowing the cooldown store to grow without the planned cap.
findings.fix: Bound the number and length of persisted keys and entries, and refuse the write explicitly if the resulting serialized file would exceed 16 KiB.
findings.reason: Already decided by the plan (§8, same finding rejected at the plan gate): the keys are a closed set of four plus one per configured unknown agy model, an entry is at most ~600 bytes, every write prunes expired entries and S20 holds the file under 16 KiB; 27+ distinct unknown agy models all spent inside one reset window is not a configuration anyone has. A cap/refusal policy is a design change, out of scope for this branch.

findings.title: Quota probes run serially and delay the round summary by up to 30 seconds per key.
findings.why: After reviewer launches finish, `DecidedAsync` awaits each key in turn. With 10 distinct spent Antigravity keys whose `/quota` probes each time out, the round waits up to five extra minutes before `RoundEngine` can produce its summary, with no progress indication during that wait.
findings.fix: Bound the probe phase with a shared deadline or run independent per-key probes concurrently, and surface that post-round quota checking is still in progress while the summary is pending.
findings.reason: By design and bounded (plan §8): one agy /quota child per SPENT key per round, each bounded at 30 s by the launcher; only spent agy refusals probe, and the table has three known keys. Running them concurrently or adding progress output is a design change outside the plan; the completed results are not affected by the wait.

findings.title: Cooldown checks synchronously reread the JSON file for each row and repeated roster decision.
findings.why: With 100 configured providers, each call to `CoolingOf` invokes `Standing`, which reads and deserializes the cooldown file. `CanRun`, exclusion construction, and provider status can each repeat this work, causing hundreds of synchronous file reads on a single request or round setup as the roster grows.
findings.fix: Read the cooldown entries once per operation and use that snapshot for its row decisions, while keeping snapshots fresh between operations so expired entries become eligible.
findings.reason: By design (plan §8): the file is read on every decision on purpose so that a park by another coai-mcp process on the same data directory is seen on the next round and an expired entry becomes eligible with no write. The file is under 16 KiB; a snapshot or mtime cache would reintroduce staleness across processes. Minor performance remark, no defect.

findings.title: AgyError splits whole stderr into substring slices per line, creating O(N²) substring allocations on multi-line errors
findings.why: When parsing stderr that contains many lines or large logs, `AgyError.Parse` does `lines = stdErr.Split('\n')` and then for every matching index performs `string.Join('\n', lines[index..])`. If a process emits stderr with thousands of lines or successive AGY_ERROR markers, joining slices repeatedly produces massive string copies and allocations, risking LOH churn and garbage collector stalls on Native-AOT runs.
findings.fix: Locate markers directly in `stdErr` using `stdErr.IndexOf("AGY_ERROR", ...)` and pass a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` or read from the offset to the end of the JSON object directly into `Utf8JsonReader` without slicing and re-joining all remaining lines.
findings.reason: Not a defect: AgyError.Parse joins the rest of stderr only for lines that START with the AGY_ERROR marker (one or two per launch) and stderr of a launch is small and bounded by the launcher; there is no input where this is quadratic in practice. Behaviour is correct and tested across both shapes and multi-line JSON.

findings.title: AgyQuotaReport.Parse splits stdout by line and reverses, re-parsing full stdout twice if stdout has no newlines
findings.why: When `stdout` is a single line, `new[] { stdout }.Concat(stdout.Split('\n').Reverse())` attempts `ParseDocument` on the exact same JSON text twice. More importantly, reversing lines to find the last valid JSON document parses arbitrary stderr/stdout lines sequentially from back to front using full UTF-8 encoding without checking line prefixes, which deviates from standard streaming parser patterns in the repo.
findings.fix: Check if `ParseDocument(stdout)` succeeds directly; only if it fails or contains trailing noise, walk backwards by line or marker and parse the trailing JSON block once.
findings.reason: Not a defect: Parse is specified as 'the whole text, else its last line that is a report' (the stream may carry a trailing line); for a single-line stdout the second attempt on the same text is a duplicate parse of a few KB, never wrong. Returns correctly in every tested shape.

findings.title: ReadEntries reads and deserializes the entire file on every decision without in-memory caching or file mtime check
findings.why: During a round and whenever provider status/roster is evaluated across stages, `CoolingOf(provider)` calls `_cooldowns.Standing(key, ...)` which invokes `ReadEntries()`. This performs synchronous disk I/O (`File.ReadAllText`) and JSON deserialization on every evaluation for every configured provider row. While the file is small (< 16 KiB), repeated disk reads per check across UI refreshes and stage decisions bypass the repository's standard pattern of timestamp-based or lease-cached state checks.
findings.fix: Check `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(JsonPath)` before reading and deserializing, or cache the in-memory `IReadOnlyList<QuotaCooldownEntry>` and invalidate when mtime advances or a local mutation occurs.
findings.reason: Same as the file-read finding: reading the file per decision is the plan's deliberate cross-process design (§8); a modification-time cache would miss a park written within the timestamp granularity by a sibling process. Minor, no defect.

findings.title: ResetFor crashes with InvalidOperationException when all spent buckets have past or equal reset times
findings.why: In `Picked()`, `var known = spent.Where(bucket => bucket.ResetTime > nowUtc).ToList();` filters spent buckets whose reset time is in the future. However, if all spent buckets have `ResetTime == null` OR their `ResetTime <= nowUtc` (for example, clocks slightly skewed, past reset timestamp returned by vendor, or exact match), `known` is empty and `Picked()` correctly returns `SpentWithoutReset`. But when at least one spent bucket has `ResetTime > nowUtc` and another spent bucket has `ResetTime <= nowUtc` (or null), `unknown` is non-empty (`spent.Except(known)`). If any bucket in `spent` has `ResetTime == null`, `spent.Where(bucket => bucket.ResetTime > nowUtc)` excludes it from `known`. However, if `known` has at least one item, `Picked` constructs `QuotaGauge.Spent` by evaluating `known.Max(bucket => bucket.ResetTime!.Value)`. But consider when `spent` contains only buckets with `ResetTime <= nowUtc`: `known.Count == 0`, returning `SpentWithoutReset`. Now consider when `spent` contains one bucket with future `reset_time` and another bucket with `disabled: false`, `remaining: 0`, and missing/unparseable `reset_time` (`ResetTime == null`): `unknown` contains the bucket with null `ResetTime`. If `bucket.Label` is evaluated, it works. But now consider the case where agy returns `remaining_fraction: 0` and `reset_time` is absent or malformed: `ResetTime` is null. But look at `AgyQuotaReport.cs` line 56: `new[] { stdout }.Concat(stdout.Split('\n').Reverse()).Select(ParseDocument).FirstOrDefault(report => report is not null)`. Notice `stdout.Split('\n')`! In `AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync`, agy stdout is passed to `AgyQuotaReport.Parse(result.StdOut)`. Notice in `AgyQuotaProbe.cs` line 247: `public static async Task<AgyQuotaReading> ReadAsync(...)`. If `ct` is cancelled during probe execution, `result.Cancelled ? throw new OperationCanceledException(ct) : Reading(result)`. When cancelled, `ct` throws `OperationCanceledException(ct)`. But what happens in `QuotaCooldowns.DecidedAsync` (line 200)? `DecidedAsync` iterates `keyed`. In `DecidedKeyAsync` (line 219), `Refusal` is evaluated. If multiple models fail on the same key or different keys, `DecidedKeyAsync` calls `ResetOfAsync`. In `QuotaCooldowns.cs` line 249: `var limited = (ReviewerOutcome.RateLimited)refused.Outcome;`. Wait, `refused.Invocation.Adapter`! In `DecidedAsync` line 199: `group.Key.Length > 0`. In `Refusal(group)` line 226: `refused` is `(ReviewerInvocation Invocation, ReviewerOutcome Outcome)`. What if `refused.Invocation.Adapter` is null? In `ReviewerInvocation`, `Adapter` is `IReviewerRuntime?`. Look at `QuotaCooldowns.cs` line 252: `await refused.Invocation.Adapter!.ReadResetAsync(...)`! If `refused.Invocation.Adapter` is null (e.g., custom invocation constructed without adapter), it throws `NullReferenceException`.
findings.fix: Safely check `refused.Invocation.Adapter` or ensure null-safe invocation when reading reset.
findings.reason: Wrong; opened the code. (a) ResetFor/Picked: known = spent buckets whose ResetTime > nowUtc, a comparison that is false for null, so every element of known has a non-null ResetTime and known.Max(b => b.ResetTime!.Value) cannot throw; an empty known returns SpentWithoutReset, and unknown buckets are named in the text (S9-S13 cover past, null and mixed resets). (b) Adapter!: DecidedAsync groups by Adapter?.QuotaKeyOf(...) ?? string.Empty and drops keys of length 0, so a result with a null Adapter never reaches ResetOfAsync. (c) AgyQuotaProbe cancellation is handled by AfterRoundAsync's OperationCanceledException catch (S42, 74312833). No crash path exists.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse does not normalize Windows CRLF line endings, breaking JSON extraction on Windows
findings.why:
In `AgyError.Parse`: `var lines = stdErr.Split('
');`. On Windows, agy output or standard error strings contain `
`. `lines[index]` will retain trailing ``. In `ReadFrom`, `var body = text.TrimStart()[Marker.Length..].TrimStart(' ', '	', ':');`. When `string.Join('
', lines[index..])` is run or when `body` is sliced, if the JSON was on a single line ending in ``, `Utf8JsonReader` with `JsonDocument.ParseValue` might parse it, but if lines are joined with `
` while preserving ``, or if `body` contains `` after the JSON, `ParseValue` consumes the object. However, `lines[index]` being split only on `
` leaves `` at the end of each line. More critically, in `AgyQuotaReport.cs` line 57: `new[] { stdout }.Concat(stdout.Split('
').Reverse()).Select(ParseDocument)...`. If `stdout` ends with `
`, splitting by `
` produces trailing `` on each line, meaning `ParseDocument` attempts `JsonDocument.Parse(text)` where `text` ends with ``. While System.Text.Json tolerates trailing whitespace in `JsonDocument.Parse`, in `AgyError.cs` line 47 `body.StartsWith('{')` expects `{` as first non-whitespace char after colon, which works if trimmed of spaces/tabs/colons, but if `` precedes `{` on a newline it fails to parse.
findings.fix:
Use `stdErr.Replace("
", "
").Split('

findings.reason: Wrong; opened the code. The marker line is found with TrimStart().StartsWith, so a trailing \r on the line does not matter; in both observed shapes the '{' follows the marker on the SAME line (body = text after 'AGY_ERROR' minus spaces/tabs/colon starts with '{'), and the following lines are handed to Utf8JsonReader/JsonDocument.ParseValue, for which \r is JSON whitespace. CRLF input therefore parses; no change needed.

findings.title: AtomicFile.Write to dataDir throws DirectoryNotFoundException if directory does not exist during unparked reads or direct writes
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.Locked`, `Directory.CreateDirectory(dataDir)` is called before taking the lock. However, in `ReadEntries()`, `File.Exists(JsonPath)` is checked without creating `dataDir`, which is safe. But if `Locked` is invoked when `dataDir` does not exist, `Directory.CreateDirectory(dataDir)` runs. Yet in `AtomicFile.Write(JsonPath, ...)`, `AtomicFile.Write` writes to a `.tmp` file in `Path.GetDirectoryName(path)` and moves it. If `JsonPath` directory is removed or permissions fail, it throws `IOException`/`UnauthorizedAccessException` which `Locked` catches, but `Applied` runs inside `Locked` without catching `IOException` directly—it relies on `Locked` catching it. However, notice `Applied` is passed to `Held(taken, body)`. Inside `Held`: `using (taken.Stream) { return body(); }`. `body()` is `Applied(ops)`. In `Locked`: `try { Directory.CreateDirectory(dataDir); return HeldFile.TakeWithin(...) switch { Hold.Taken taken => Held(taken, body)... } } catch (Exception failure) when (failure is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)`. Notice: if `AtomicFile.Write` inside `body()` throws `IOException`, `Held` does not catch it; the exception unwinds to `Locked`'s catch block, which returns `new CooldownWrite.Refused(Describe(failure))`. But `taken.Stream` is disposed during unwinding! Wait, what about `HeldFile.TakeWithin`? When `Held.Taken` is returned, `taken.Stream` is a `FileStream` holding a lock on `quota-cooldowns.lock`. On Windows, if `AtomicFile.Write` attempts to replace or write in the same directory while another stream is open or temporary files are created, it works. But look at `Applied` at line 287: `if (next.SequenceEqual(current)) return new CooldownWrite.Written();`. `QuotaCooldownEntry` is a record class. Does `SequenceEqual` compare by value? Yes, records implement value equality. But look at `current`: `current` is read by `ReadEntries()` BEFORE `InLock("read")`. `current` was read outside the lock before, and then re-read inside `Applied`: `var current = ReadEntries();`. Notice `ReadEntries()` at line 324: `.Select(entry => entry with { Model = entry.Model ?? string.Empty, Note = entry.Note ?? string.Empty })`. In `ParkOp.Applied`, `SinceUtc` is set to `standing?.SinceUtc ?? now`. When `JsonSerializer.Serialize` runs, `DateTimeOffset` precision in JSON is formatted according to standard ISO (usually up to 7 decimal digits or rounded). When deserialized back from JSON, sub-millisecond or sub-tick precision might differ from in-memory `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, causing `next.SequenceEqual(current)` to evaluate false even if identical.
findings.fix: Ensure `SinceUtc` and `UntilUtc` truncations match serialized JSON precision (e.g. truncated to milliseconds or seconds) to avoid unnecessary file writes.
findings.reason: Wrong: System.Text.Json writes and reads DateTimeOffset at full 100-ns tick precision (round-trip 'O' form), so a value written and re-read compares equal; and SinceUtc/UntilUtc are normalised to UTC. Even if they differed the only effect would be one redundant atomic write, never a lost or wrong cooldown. The IOException/UnauthorizedAccess path is caught in Locked and returns Refused (S37).

findings.title: Raw error string from file operations leaked into user-facing ServerNotice
findings.why: In `QuotaCooldowns.Mutate`, when `written` is `CooldownWrite.Refused refused`, line 262 executes: `Tell($"A spent quota could not be remembered ({refused.Why}); the next round may launch the spent model again.");`. `refused.Why` contains `Describe(failure)` from `Locked`, which is `${failure.GetType().Name}: ${failure.Message}` (line 319). On file system errors (e.g., permission denied, path not found), internal filesystem paths from `failure.Message` (e.g., `/home/.../quota-cooldowns.json.tmp`) are directly formatted into `ServerNotice.Detail`. Per the project rules and security guidelines (error messages don't leak sensitive data/paths to UI), raw exception messages containing server-internal paths should not be directly exposed in user notices.
findings.fix: Sanitize or summarize `refused.Why` before passing it to `Tell()` and the `ServerNotice` detail.
findings.reason: Out of scope and by design: the notice (plan D4, S37) exists to tell the operator of THIS data directory why a park could not be remembered, so it names the cause; it goes through ServerNotice.Shortened, the shared helper that cuts it, and it reaches the local panel, not an outside party. Redacting the exception text would remove the only diagnosis the operator has.

findings.title: Uncached disk reads and JSON parsing of quota file on hot path during roster building and provider status queries
findings.why: CanRun, ExclusionReason, and ProvidersAsync call CoolingOf for every configured provider row. CoolingOf calls _cooldowns.Standing(key), which synchronously executes File.ReadAllText and JsonSerializer.Deserialize on disk. In a configuration with 10-20 models polled every 10 seconds (or during multi-stage roster evaluation across dozens of candidates), this performs redundant filesystem reads and JSON deserializations for every single provider check rather than reading once per cycle or caching the parsed cooldown set in memory.
findings.fix: Cache the parsed QuotaCooldownFile in memory inside QuotaCooldowns with a file modification timestamp check or reload on mutation, so repeated queries across providers and poll ticks reuse the in-memory state without re-reading and re-parsing disk JSON on every provider check.
findings.reason: Duplicate of the file-read finding: deliberate per-decision read (plan §8), a file under 16 KiB read a handful of times per round or panel poll; no defect.

findings.title: Subarray string concatenation in a LINQ loop allocates O(N^2) strings when parsing stderr
findings.why: In AgyError.Parse, Enumerable.Range iterates through lines and for every matching line executes string.Join('\n', lines[index..]), allocating a slice and re-joining the entire remainder of stderr into a newly allocated string just to pass to ReadFrom. If stderr contains large outputs or many error lines, this repeatedly duplicates and reallocates substantial strings in memory.
findings.fix: Pass the original stderr string and the index or substring start to ReadFrom directly instead of rejoining array slices with string.Join.
findings.reason: Duplicate of the AgyError allocation finding: one or two markers per launch on small stderr; not a defect.

findings.title: Refused quota write notice omits actionable user guidance on file permission or lock contention
findings.why: When Mutate fails to acquire the lock or write the file, Tell produces 'A spent quota could not be remembered ({refused.Why}); the next round may launch the spent model again.' If the cause is a stale lock file or permission issue on quota-cooldowns.lock, the message names the internal symptom but does not instruct the user or admin how to clear the wedged lock or fix directory permissions.
findings.fix: Include remediation guidance in the notice message (e.g. indicating whether to inspect file permissions or check for dangling quota-cooldowns.lock processes).
findings.reason: Not a defect: there is no stale lock to clear (plan §8: the lock is released with its handle, nothing is left to sweep) and the notice already states the cause and the consequence (the next round may launch the spent model again). Adding remediation prose is a wording preference outside the plan.

findings.title: §12 leaves a restored account parked until its saved reset expires, despite D4 promising an answered launch can lift it
findings.why: If someone re-logs in or buys a plan while a quota cooldown is standing, `CanRun` excludes every row sharing that key, so no launch can succeed and trigger `Lift`. The explicitly recorded outcome is that the account remains unavailable until the old gauge or estimate time, possibly days later; there is no user-facing recovery path in this plan.
findings.fix: Add a reachable recovery action in this scope—such as a successful check or a clearly defined try-now action that lifts the key—and specify its UI, effect, and tests; otherwise remove the claimed success-based lift and state the actual recovery contract.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The lift being unreachable through a round is a known, recorded cost: plan D12 and §12 last item; the later plan adds the road. Noted for the code round.)

findings.title: §4 and §7 verify lock contention only between handles in one process, not the promised cross-process safety
findings.why: If two `coai-mcp` processes share the data directory, S35–S37's two-store, one-process setup may not reproduce the operating system's locking behavior for separate processes. A lock implementation that only coordinates in-process handles could pass these checks while the two processes overwrite each other's parks or lifts, contradicting D4's multi-process guarantee.
findings.fix: Add a test that starts two independent processes against one data directory and interleaves park/lift operations, or narrow the guarantee if the chosen lock primitive cannot be verified this way.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Per-handle contention is the plan's stated, chosen test method; HeldFile's exclusive open is per handle.)

findings.title: §4 and §7 do not verify recovery from a process killed during a locked aggregate write
findings.why: If the server is killed after acquiring the lock or while publishing the aggregate, the plan relies on the handle releasing the lock and `AtomicFile.Write` preserving the prior file, but its tests cover interleaving and a malformed file rather than a kill at that boundary. A regression that leaves subsequent writers blocked or damages the prior cooldown state would not be caught.
findings.fix: Add a process-level interruption scenario that kills a writer during the mutation and verifies a later writer can acquire the lock and the JSON is either the prior or complete new aggregate.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: §3 D4, §3 D12: Cooldown lift and guess-doubling are dead code in practice because CanRun permanently excludes all rows of a cooling key from running
findings.why: D4 and S18/S25 specify that an answered launch ending in Ok lifts a standing cooldown (e.g. following re-login or quota top-up), and D5 specifies that consecutive guess intervals double upon subsequent launches. However, D9 specifies that CanRun checks '&& !IsCooling(provider)'. If a row's key is cooling, RosterBuilder never schedules that row, so no round can ever launch the model while cooling. Consequently, no launch can ever return Ok to trigger Lift(), and no second attempt can launch to double the guess interval. A user who tops up their quota or re-authenticates is permanently locked out until untilUtc expires (which may be up to a week for agy-weekly), unless an out-of-band mechanism exists, which the plan defers to D12.
findings.fix: Either document that cooldowns cannot be cleared by rounds and rely strictly on natural expiration, or provide an active probing / manual check mechanism in this plan (e.g., during explicit UI check/probe actions) rather than deferring the only functional recovery path to a future plan.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (Same known item as finding 0: D12 and §12 record it; noted for the code round.)

findings.title: §3 D5, §3 D6: Ambiguous conflict resolution when a quota probe returns Available for a key with an explicitly spent outcome
findings.why: In D5, the plan states: 'An explicitly spent refusal (Spent == true) whose gauge answers Available is parked on stated/guess all the same (the refusal is the newer fact and the vendor's own field), and the note names the contradiction (S41).' However, D6 states under ResetFor: 'Available (every active, readable bucket's remaining_fraction > 0)'. If ResetFor returns Available, it does not return an untilUtc or reset instant. A reviewer or developer implementing ReadResetAsync based on D6's outcome enum will have no reset timestamp from the probe to construct a QuotaReset, leaving it undefined how ReadResetAsync falls back to stated/guess when ResetFor evaluates to Available.
findings.fix: Specify in D6/ReadResetAsync that when ResetFor returns Available but the outcome had Spent == true, ReadResetAsync explicitly falls back to CooldownParser.StatedReset(reason, nowUtc) or CooldownParser.Fallback(reason, consecutive).
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here. (The code already does the fallback: QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs falls back to the text reset when Spent==true and the gauge reads Available, S41.)

findings.title: §3 D8, §3 D9: Inconsistent date formatting and missing year in cooldown line specification
findings.why: D8 states the card displays dates formatted as 'dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm' (e.g. 14.10.2026 09:19). But in D9 and S32, the guess wording example is given as 'quota spent — reset time unknown; next try 11.10.2026 19:00 (in 30 min)' whereas D9 earlier gives 'quota spent — reset time unknown; next try 11.10. 17:00' without the year. An automated test checking exact string matches across the three sources (quota vs stated vs guess) could fail or introduce inconsistent date layouts across cards.
findings.fix: Standardize all date template specifications in D9 to explicitly include the 4-digit year 'dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm', matching D8 and S31/S32.
findings.reason: The plan is frozen for this change: it passed its own plan gate before the code was written, and this branch implements it as committed; a plan change is out of scope here.

findings.title: QuotaCooldowns is split with a partial instead of an extracted unit
findings.why: The change declares `QuotaCooldowns` as `partial` here and adds its round logic in `QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs`. The project rule says: “Extract utilities from large modules; split by extracting a named unit with its own responsibility, never a `partial` (or its equivalent) to duck the limit”.
findings.fix: Move the round-specific behavior into a named unit with its own responsibility, and have it use `QuotaCooldowns` through an explicit interface or API rather than extending the class with `partial`.

findings.title: Cooldown writes have no bound on the number or size of retained entries
findings.why: Each previously unseen Antigravity model gets its own unknown-family key, and every live entry is retained on later writes. With enough distinct models, the serialized file can exceed the plan’s 16 KiB limit; subsequent reads and round writes then keep processing the oversized file, undermining the promised bounded durable store.
findings.fix: Before replacing the file, enforce a total serialized-size limit and refuse the write through the existing refusal path if the aggregate would exceed it; also bound or validate entry fields read from disk.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's contract: plan §8 sets the budget (one entry per key, keys come only from rows a person configures, under ten in any real settings file; notes capped at 400 chars; every write drops expired entries) and the gate accepted it. Keys are never taken from vendor or network input, so nothing external can grow the file; the file lives in the user's own data dir.

findings.title: Quota probes run serially, so distinct spent keys can add minutes after the reviews finish
findings.why: When a round has ten distinct Antigravity model IDs from unlisted families, `QuotaKeyOf` gives each its own key and `MovesAsync` awaits each `/quota` probe in sequence. If each probe reaches the 30-second timeout, the round summary is delayed by up to five minutes after reviewer work has ended, with no progress indication from this loop.
findings.fix: Run independent per-key probes concurrently with a bounded degree of parallelism, then apply their moves in one aggregate write.

findings.title: AgyQuotaGroups routes Claude and GPT models to Antigravity in direct violation of mandatory vendor routing
findings.why: Table entry `new(AgyQuotaKeys.ThirdParty, ["claude-opus-5-5", "claude-sonnet-5-5", "gpt-oss-120b"], ["3p-weekly", "3p-5h"])` explicitly configures Claude models on Antigravity. Rule `.agents/rules/common/vendor-routing.md` states: 'A Claude model runs through the claude CLI. Never through agy, never through codex.' and under Constraints: 'local.common.vendor-routing: a Claude model never runs on agy.'
findings.fix: Remove Claude models (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`) from `AgyQuotaGroups` under `antigravity/3p` and map only models permitted to run on agy (such as GPT-OSS), or ensure Claude models are rejected rather than mapped to an agy quota group.
findings.reason: Wrong: plan D3 specifies this exact table row (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, gpt-oss-120b -> antigravity/3p) from the measured `agy models` list, and says vendor-routing still forbids a Claude model on agy. A quota-key mapping routes nothing and launches nothing; routing is enforced where rows are built. The row exists so that an agy row configured against the rule still gets its own key instead of falling to Gemini.

findings.title: Mutable dictionary updated in-place violates immutability doctrine
findings.why: In `WriteUnderLock`, mutable `Dictionary<string, QuotaCooldownEntry>` is modified via `table.Remove(lift.Key)` and `table[park.Key] = ...`. `.agents/conventions/common/coding-style.md` mandates: 'ALWAYS create new objects, NEVER mutate existing ones: WRONG: modify(original, field, value) -> changes original in-place; CORRECT: update(original, field, value) -> returns new copy with change. Immutable data prevents hidden side effects, makes debugging easier, and enables safe concurrency.' and `.agents/conventions/csharp/doctrine.md` §7: 'Never mutate; return a new value.'
findings.fix: Construct a new immutable dictionary or collection for each move operation (e.g., using `table.SetItem()` or building a new dictionary / LINQ transformation) rather than mutating `table` in place.
findings.reason: Wrong reading of the rule: `table` is a local builder created inside WriteUnderLock from the freshly re-read file, under the lock, and is never shared, returned or exposed; the doctrine's immutability concerns shared values and contracts. The result is serialised into a new file; no hidden side effect or concurrency hazard exists. Rewriting it as an immutable-dictionary chain adds allocation for no safety gain.

findings.title: Mutable List<T> used in internal record contract instead of immutable IReadOnlyList<T>
findings.why: `internal sealed record QuotaCooldownFile(int V, List<QuotaCooldownRecord>? Entries);` exposes `List<T>`. `.agents/conventions/csharp/doctrine.md` §7 states: 'Never mutate; return a new value. Public contracts expose IReadOnlyList<T> { get; init; } defaulting to [], never List<T> { get; set; }.'
findings.fix: Change `List<QuotaCooldownRecord>? Entries` to `IReadOnlyList<QuotaCooldownRecord>? Entries` on `QuotaCooldownFile`.
findings.reason: Wrong target: doctrine section 7 is about PUBLIC contracts. QuotaCooldownFile is an internal source-generated JSON shape that is deserialised once and immediately normalised into an IReadOnlyList of entries (Entries()); it is not a contract anyone holds.

findings.title: QuotaKeyOf uses invocation.Adapter instead of row runtime, routing all adapter-less runtimes to an empty key
findings.why: KeyOf extracts the quota key via `pair.Invocation.Adapter?.QuotaKeyOf(pair.Invocation.Model)`. In ConnectOtherAIs, reviewer adapters and runtimes are distinct abstractions; runtimes implementing IReviewerRuntime like KimiRuntime or CodexRuntime are often resolved or wrapped in ReviewerRuntime without Invocation.Adapter being set (or set to null for generic/API/custom runtime paths). When Invocation.Adapter is null or does not implement IReviewerRuntime (e.g., KimiRuntime which defines QuotaKeyOf directly on the runtime class rather than through an adapter reference on Invocation), KeyOf evaluates to string.Empty. Results for that runtime are discarded at line 153 (`.Where(keyed => keyed.Key.Length > 0)`), meaning rate limit exhaustion for that runtime is never grouped, never parked, and never cooled down.
findings.fix: Resolve the quota key via the row's IReviewerRuntime instance (or provide a unified lookup on ReviewerInvocation / runtime resolution) rather than relying exclusively on nullable Invocation.Adapter.
findings.reason: Wrong: ReviewerInvocation.Adapter IS the row's runtime (IReviewerRuntime), set to `this` by every runtime that builds an invocation (Codex/Claude/Antigravity at ReviewerRuntime.cs:689,871, ClaudeRuntime.cs:114, AntigravityRuntime.cs:72) and to Bound(settings), itself a KimiRuntime that defines QuotaKeyOf (KimiRuntime.cs:64,126). The executor classifies every outcome through the same field. Only Local/Api/Remote leave it null, and D3 gives those the empty key on purpose. TheRoundParksAndLiftsTheQuotaTests parks codex, claude and kimi through exactly this path.

findings.title: PanelService creates a second uncoordinated QuotaCooldowns instance disconnected from RoundEngine
findings.why: PanelService instantiates `_cooldowns = new QuotaCooldowns(...)` at line 109 and passes it down into RoundEngine. However, if any other part of the system or background worker inspects or writes cooldowns or if multiple instances of PanelService exist across lifetime scopes, each instance manages its own lock wait and in-memory notification callbacks independently. Furthermore, `StandingFor` in PanelService directly calls `_cooldowns.Standing(key, _clock.GetUtcNow())` reading disk on every single roster/exclusion check for every provider row without any cache or sharing with engine run state, coupling the presentation/RPC layer directly to file-system reads instead of domain state.
findings.fix: Pass the QuotaCooldowns service as a shared dependency into PanelService or consolidate cooldown query state within an established domain component rather than having PanelService instantiate and poll disk across each provider evaluation.
findings.reason: Wrong: PanelService creates ONE QuotaCooldowns (PanelService.cs:109) and passes that same instance to RoundEngine (PanelService.cs:153); there is no second instance. Reading the file on every CanRun with no cache is plan D4's stated decision (file under 16 KiB for ever).

findings.title: Table mapping in AgyQuotaGroups is closed and leaks model family strings across layers
findings.why: AgyQuotaGroups hardcodes specific model string literals (`gemini-3.8-flash`, `claude-opus-5-5`, etc.) directly inside runners/Reviewers instead of deriving from the configuration or runtime registration. When new models are added to Antigravity, any model name not explicitly enumerated falls back to `antigravity/?` + id. When that happens, BucketIdsOf returns empty list (`[]`), causing `ResetFor` to always return `GroupMissing` and preventing `/quota` probe readings from ever detecting bucket exhaustion or reset timestamps for those models.
findings.fix: Make AgyQuotaGroups allow matching bucket IDs by model family or register quota group mappings dynamically from provider capabilities so new model variants automatically map to their respective bucket quotas.
findings.reason: Outside the plan's scope and contrary to it: D3 deliberately chose one explicit, measured table over a prefix or dynamic rule, because a `gemini-` prefix would park every Gemini row when only Argon is spent; an unknown family gets its own key and no inferred group. Adding a family is one table row with its fixture.

findings.title: Utf8JsonReader over multi-line payload throws on unconsumed trailing lines or fails to parse trailing json tokens
findings.why: In `AgyError.LineOf`, `Utf8JsonReader` is initialized over UTF-8 bytes of `payload`, which is formed in `Payload` by joining the `AGY_ERROR` line with all subsequent lines of `stderr` (`string.Join('\n', ...)`). If stderr contains multi-line output or subsequent output lines, `JsonDocument.TryParseValue(ref reader, out var document)` parses the first JSON value, but if the JSON payload is malformed or followed by arbitrary non-JSON stderr lines, `Utf8JsonReader` or `JsonDocument.TryParseValue` throws `JsonException` before completing when looking ahead across buffer boundaries or encounters invalid tokens in the joined buffer, causing legitimate `AGY_ERROR` lines to return `null` and drop structured error classification.
findings.fix: Pass only the balanced JSON object substring or parse lines incrementally rather than blindly appending all remaining stderr lines into the buffer passed to Utf8JsonReader.
findings.reason: Wrong: AgyError.LineOf wraps the read in a catch of JsonException/InvalidOperationException and returns null; JsonDocument.TryParseValue stops after the FIRST JSON value, so the following stderr lines are never read as tokens. AnErrorObjectPrintedOverSeveralLines_IsReadLikeOneOnASingleLine (review fix R5) pins a pretty-printed object with trailing stderr lines.

findings.title: WriteUnderLock disposes lockFile without releasing or unlinking HeldFile lock
findings.why: `WriteUnderLock` begins with `using var held = lockFile;`. When `HeldFile.TakeWithin` returns a `FileStream`, wrapping it in `using var held` disposes the stream when `WriteUnderLock` exits. However, `HeldFile` relies on file locking semantics, and if `WriteUnderLock` encounters an error or returns, disposing `lockFile` is performed, but if caller or nested methods expect `Hold` to manage disposal, or if `AtomicFile.Write` operates while other handles exist, double disposal or stale file lock descriptors can block subsequent `TakeWithin` attempts on platforms where locks are advisory or handle inheritance locks the path.
findings.fix: Ensure `Hold` / `FileStream` ownership and disposal semantics strictly adhere to `HeldFile`'s contract, disposing only through the `Hold` abstraction.
findings.reason: Wrong: HeldFile's contract is that Hold.Taken carries the FileStream and the holder releases the lock by disposing it (HeldFile.cs:44,126,187 do exactly that). `using var held = lockFile` is the single disposal; nothing else disposes it and nothing unlinks the lock file (D4: never deleted).

findings.title: Uncaught OperationCanceledException during quota probe throws instead of fail-safe handling
findings.why: In `ReadQuotaAsync`, `catch (Exception e) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)` catches exceptions to return `AgyQuotaRead.Cannot(...)`, but if `ct.IsCancellationRequested` is true, the exception is rethrown. If a round's token is cancelled while probing, `AfterRoundAsync` catches `OperationCanceledException`, but if called via `ReadResetAsync` directly from another caller without an outer try-catch, the cancellation aborts unexpectedly.
findings.fix: Ensure `ReadResetAsync` callers handle cancellation gracefully or document that cancellation bubbles up deliberately.
findings.reason: By design, already stated in the doc comment and the plan (D5 Cancellation): the round's own cancel reaches the caller of ReadResetAsync, and the only caller, AfterRoundAsync, catches OperationCanceledException and logs. Not gating, no failing input exists.

findings.title: Synchronous file I/O on hot CanRun filter reads and deserializes JSON repeatedly without caching
findings.why: StandingFor calls QuotaCooldowns.Standing(key, now) for every provider during roster construction and provider enumeration. QuotaCooldowns.Standing executes File.ReadAllText and JsonSerializer.Deserialize from disk synchronously every time without any caching or in-memory snapshot. When provider lists or roster checks are filtered across multiple stages and reviewer evaluations (e.g., 10x providers or repeated status polling), this triggers dozens of redundant disk reads and JSON parsing passes on hot paths.
findings.fix: Hold an in-memory snapshot of QuotaCooldownFile or live entries with a file-version/timestamp check or update it upon WriteUnderLock, or cache entries for the duration of a round/provider scan rather than performing unbuffered disk I/O on every CanRun check.
findings.reason: Plan D4 decides this explicitly: read on every CanRun, no cache, because the file is under 16 KiB for ever and several coai-mcp processes share it, so a cache would hide another process's park (the cross-process contract of S35-S37). Plan is frozen.

findings.title: Sequential /quota CLI invocations block round completion instead of querying in parallel
findings.why: In MovesAsync, foreach (var group in Groups(results)) awaits MoveAsync sequentially. Each MoveAsync for a refused key invokes AgyQuotaProbe.ReadAsync, which spawns an external process with a 30s timeout. If multiple Antigravity quotas or distinct keys fail in a round, the post-round processing waits serially for each CLI probe (e.g. 3 distinct quota keys taking up to 90s total), adding unnecessary latency to round termination while the user waits for the verdict.
findings.fix: Run MoveAsync across distinct groups concurrently with Task.WhenAll(groups.Select(g => MoveAsync(...))) before aggregating the resulting moves for Record.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse allocates strings and re-parses JSON over all lines of stderr
findings.why: Parse splits the entire stderr by newline and constructs a joined substring array (Payload) using string.Join for every line starting with AGY_ERROR, re-allocating UTF-8 bytes with Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(payload) for Utf8JsonReader on each match. For long stderrs or multiple error lines, this creates unnecessary string and byte allocations on the failure evaluation path.
findings.fix: Pass a ReadOnlySpan<char> or byte span directly to Utf8JsonReader or parse the stream without intermediate string.Join and byte-array allocations.
findings.reason: Negligible and unmeasured: Parse runs once per failed agy launch on a stderr of a few lines; no failure scenario exists.

findings.title: `AgyQuotaGroups` reimplements a runtime-name table outside the shared source of truth
findings.why: The project rule says, “A decision that must hold everywhere belongs in the function everyone calls, not in each caller.” This new explicit table is what maps Antigravity models to quota groups, but it lives in `AgyQuotaGroups` rather than an existing shared runtime/model-family decision seam. Other code paths can make routing decisions without consulting it, so the same model-family decision can diverge.
findings.fix: Put the quota-group mapping on the existing shared model-family decision seam and have quota-key lookup use that single implementation.
findings.reason: Outside the plan and already decided in round 1: plan D3 chose one explicit, measured table in its own file (AgyQuotaGroups) and every caller (PanelService, QuotaRound, the agy runtime) goes through its single KeyOf/NameOf. The finding names no existing 'shared model-family seam' that routing uses; none exists for quota groups.

findings.title: Cooldown writes do not enforce the 16 KiB file limit
findings.why: If enough distinct quota keys are parked—for example, many configured unknown Antigravity models, each with a note near the 400-character limit—`Serialized` writes every live entry without checking the resulting size, so the durable file can exceed the plan's 16 KiB bound and continue growing across rounds.
findings.fix: Check the serialized byte length before replacement and refuse the write with the existing warning and notice path when it exceeds 16 KiB.
findings.reason: Already decided in round 1: plan §8 budget (one entry per key, keys come only from configured rows, notes capped at 400 chars, every write drops expired entries; the 16 KiB figure is the ceiling S20 checks, not a runtime gate). Marked Minor/non-gating by the reviewer itself; no new argument.

findings.title: A finished review round waits for quota probes before returning its summary
findings.why: When a round has a spent refusal, `AfterRoundAsync` awaits the `/quota` probes before building the summary. If an agy probe hangs, the configured 30-second timeout adds that wait after reviewers have finished, while the person sees the round still in progress without any indication that quota checking is the remaining step.
findings.fix: Expose the quota-check phase in the round's existing progress/status updates, or make the probe non-blocking for summary delivery and record its result afterward.
findings.reason: Outside the plan: D5 puts the parking between RunAllAsync and the summary on purpose, and the wait is now bounded by ONE 30 s probe timeout (the probes of distinct keys run together since 6927d17b) and only when a round ends with a spent refusal. A new progress phase or a deferred summary is a design change the plan did not ask for.

findings.title: PanelService binds cooldown lookups to ProviderSettings.Model instead of the resolved model
findings.why: When a provider row specifies an empty model string or a model alias/override resolved dynamically at execution time, StandingFor uses provider.Model directly (''). AgyQuotaGroups.KeyOf maps empty string to AntigravityRuntime.DefaultModel ('antigravity/gemini'). However, for non-antigravity providers or rows where resolution logic applies, or if a custom row omits the model property in settings, QuotaKeyOf is evaluated on the raw unvalidated string. More critically, ReviewerInvocation generated during the round uses the resolved model, causing QuotaRound to park under the resolved model's key while CanRun and StandingFor check the un-resolved provider.Model string, leading to key mismatch where CanRun fails to exclude the parked row.
findings.fix: Resolve provider.Model through the same model-resolution seam used when creating ReviewerInvocation before calling runtime.QuotaKeyOf(model) in PanelService.StandingFor.
findings.reason: Wrong: the roster builds its invocation with the same raw string, `Model = provider.Model` (RosterBuilder.cs:529), that StandingFor passes to QuotaKeyOf, and QuotaRound keys on invocation.Model, which is that value. Parked and queried keys are the same string, and an empty model resolves to the runtime default on both sides inside AgyQuotaGroups.KeyOf. No second resolution step exists to diverge from.

findings.title: Lift check uses un-isolated unlocked store.Standing() instead of relying on transactional locked evaluation
findings.why: In MoveAsync, a successful reviewer outcome (ReviewerOutcome.Ok) checks `store.Standing(key, now) is not null` outside of any file lock before deciding to issue `QuotaMove.Lift(key)`. If an entry is written or expires concurrently between the round's pre-filter check and locked application, or if multiple workers/rounds evaluate lifts, performing an unlocked check to gate generation of QuotaMove.Lift causes valid lifting events to be dropped if Standing() read was slightly torn or stale. More importantly, it leaks the storage state read into the round planning phase, violating the boundary where QuotaMove expresses aggregate intent and Apply executes the state transition atomically under lock.
findings.fix: Emit QuotaMove.Lift(key) whenever group.Any(pair => pair.Outcome is ReviewerOutcome.Ok), and let Change/table.Remove handle idempotently under lock.
findings.reason: Already decided (review fix R3): the unlocked Standing read only decides whether a Lift is worth a lock at all, so a round with nothing to lift takes no lock; the locked re-read still decides under the lock, and Lift of a key that is not there is a no-op. Emitting a Lift for every Ok would take the lock (and risk a refused-lock notice) on every ordinary round. The residual race (a park by another process between the read and the write) was recorded in the fix notes: there is no right answer to it.

findings.title: Hopeless short-circuits on RateLimit.Hopeless when Spent is false
findings.why: The contract in plan DoD 1 states: 'RateLimitVerdict / ReviewerOutcome.RateLimited carry bool? Spent (true = vendor says spent, false = transient, null = nobody said, text read as before); BoundedScheduler.Hopeless = Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(reason)'. However, line 681 implements `(limited.Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(limited.Reason)) || RetryLadder.ResetOutlasts(...)`. If Spent is explicitly false (vendor says transient), the second operand of `||` (RetryLadder.ResetOutlasts) is still evaluated. If reason text happens to match a stated reset outlasting budget, Hopeless returns true despite the vendor explicitly marking it transient.
findings.fix: Evaluate ResetOutlasts only when Spent is not false, e.g.: `limited.Spent ?? (RateLimit.Hopeless(limited.Reason) || RetryLadder.ResetOutlasts(limited.Reason, RetryLadder.Remaining(elapsed, budget), _clock.GetUtcNow()))`.
findings.reason: Wrong against the plan: D1 says `Hopeless` becomes `limited.Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(limited.Reason)` 'the ResetOutlasts half unchanged', i.e. a stated reset that outlasts the remaining budget ends the ladder whatever the verdict said; that is exactly the behaviour AStatedResetIsNeverWaitedOutTests pins. Reviewer rates it Minor/non-gating; the fix would change the plan's decision.

findings.title: AgyQuotaGroups.KeyOf uses case-insensitive match for known families but retains original casing in fallback, creating divergent cooldown keys
findings.why: When an unknown model ID arrives (e.g. `GEMINI-custom` or `claude-3-7-sonnet`), `KeyOf` strips any effort suffix using `OrdinalIgnoreCase` but checks `Table` with `OrdinalIgnoreCase`. If it does not match, it appends the unnormalized `id` to `AgyQuotaKeys.UnknownPrefix` ('antigravity/?' + id). If subsequent calls use different casing or if a model ID is supplied in mixed casing across invocations, different cooldown keys are generated (e.g. 'antigravity/?My-Model' vs 'antigravity/?my-model'). Furthermore, `QuotaCooldowns` serializes and indexes keys case-sensitively (`StringComparer.Ordinal`). A cooldown parked under one casing will fail to match on `StandingFor` or `CanRun` when queried with another casing, causing the cooling model to not be excluded and instead be repeatedly launched and failed.
findings.fix: Normalize the model ID family/name (e.g. using `ToLowerInvariant()` or consistent invariant casing) when forming the fallback unknown quota key in `KeyOf`.
findings.reason: No failing input: a row's model string is configured once and read from the same place by CanRun/StandingFor (provider.Model) and by the round (invocation.Model = provider.Model), so the parked and the queried key are identical strings. Known families match case-insensitively to ONE key; an unknown model keeps its configured spelling as its own key, which is what 'its own key, no inferred group' (D3) asks for.

findings.title: TimeLeft throws or returns non-positive values when called right at or after expiry
findings.why: In `PanelService.TimeLeft`, `left = untilUtc - _clock.GetUtcNow()` calculates the remaining duration. Because `IsCooling` and `StandingFor` check `UntilUtc > nowUtc` at an earlier instant, by the time `CoolingSentence` and `TimeLeft` are evaluated, `_clock.GetUtcNow()` may have advanced to equal or exceed `untilUtc`. In this race/boundary condition, `left.TotalHours` and `left.TotalMinutes` become <= 0, causing `TimeLeft` to return `0 min` or negative minutes (e.g. `-0 min`), which contradicts the user-facing contract and is confusing in exclusion reports. If `untilUtc <= nowUtc`, `Math.Ceiling` produces `0 min` or negative values.
findings.fix: Clamp `left` to a minimum (e.g. `var remaining = left <= TimeSpan.Zero ? TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1) : left;`) or ensure `Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Ceiling(left.TotalMinutes))` is used when formatting.
findings.reason: Cosmetic window of less than a clock tick: StandingFor and TimeLeft read the clock one after the other, so 'in 0 min' can only appear if the entry expires between two adjacent reads, and then it is true. No input or test reaches it without a clock that jumps between two calls; the card's own text (cooldownWords.ts) already prints '' once passed. Not a defect in the plan's scope.

findings.title: AgyQuotaProbe parses stderr as raw string without redaction on non-zero exit
findings.why: In `AgyQuotaProbe.ExitReason`, `result.StdErr.Split('\n')...` extracts the first non-blank line of stderr and passes it to `VendorReason.Written(line)`. While `VendorReason.Written` is used, if `agy` outputs credentials, tokens, or sensitive context in unexpected error lines before or alongside error details during exit, and `VendorReason.Written` only redacts known patterns, unredacted raw vendor text can end up stored in cooldown records and broadcast via server notices/logs.
findings.fix: Ensure `ExitReason` strictly bounds length and applies the repository's standard secret scrubbers before storing or returning probe error text.
findings.reason: Wrong: ExitReason passes the line through VendorReason.Written, which is Redaction.SafeText (the product's one redactor: control characters, key blocks, credential-named values, recognisable shapes) cut at a cap, and the note is cut again at 400 characters. That IS 'the repository's standard secret scrubber'; no second one exists to apply.

findings.title: ProvidersAsync performs un-cached synchronous disk I/O on every provider row in an async endpoint
findings.why: When the UI or extension polls `ProvidersAsync` (which runs on a 10s timer), it evaluates `CooldownOf(provider)` and `CanRun(provider)` for each provider row. Both call `StandingFor(provider)`, which executes `_cooldowns.Standing(key, now)`. `Standing` synchronously calls `File.Exists` and `File.ReadAllText` (via `ReadFile()`) to read `quota-cooldowns.json` from disk without caching or locking. For N providers, this triggers 2*N synchronous disk reads inside an async server endpoint, blocking threadpool threads and incurring repeated filesystem I/O on hot polling paths.
findings.fix: Read `_cooldowns` once per `ProvidersAsync` request (or cache/memoize the file contents with a short TTL/mtime check in memory) so provider rows do not individually re-read and deserialize `quota-cooldowns.json` from disk multiple times per poll.
findings.reason: Already decided in round 1 (plan D4): read on every CanRun with no cache, because several coai-mcp processes share the file and a cache would hide another process's park. The file is under 16 KiB for ever, and the panel's probe refresh is every 10 s.

findings.title: AgyError.Parse allocates array slices and UTF-8 byte arrays per line on every stderr check
findings.why: In `AgyError.Parse`, every line starting with `AGY_ERROR` allocates `following` via `lines[(marked.Index + 1)..]` (an array slice copying remaining lines), concatenates strings with `string.Join`, and then encodes the payload string to bytes with `System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(payload)` to feed `Utf8JsonReader`. When stderr contains multiple lines or frequent checks run across reviewer launches, this causes unnecessary string and byte array heap allocations and array copies on the rate-limit evaluation path.
findings.fix: Avoid slicing lines array and allocating byte buffers; construct a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` or parse directly from the input buffer using `JsonDocument.Parse(string)` or single-pass span/memory slice without `string.Join` and `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes`.
findings.reason: Already rejected in round 1: Parse runs once per failed agy launch over a stderr of a few lines; no measured cost and no failing scenario. Raised again without a new argument.

findings.title: TimeLeft displays '0 min' or negative values if untilUtc is in the past or immediately expiring
findings.why: In `TimeLeft(DateTimeOffset untilUtc)`, `var left = untilUtc - _clock.GetUtcNow()` computes the remaining span. If `left.TotalHours < 1`, it returns `${Math.Ceiling(left.TotalMinutes)} min`. If `untilUtc` is equal to or slightly behind `now` (e.g. within seconds of boundary before status flips or during clock skew), `Math.Ceiling(left.TotalMinutes)` evaluates to `0` or negative values like `0 min` or `-1 min` in the exclusion sentence 'back at {at} (in 0 min)', which provides confusing DX/UX to the user.
findings.fix: Ensure `Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Ceiling(left.TotalMinutes))` is used, or check if `left <= TimeSpan.Zero` to render a clean fallback like '< 1 min' or 'now'.
findings.reason: Duplicate of finding 7 (same TimeLeft expiry-tick edge), Minor and non-gating; same reason.
